Sensini avvisa l’Inter: "Ha qualcosa in più, ma la Lazio può fare il bis"

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Sensini avvisa l’Inter: "Ha qualcosa in più, ma la Lazio può fare il bis"

Intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, l'ex difensore della Lazio Nestor Sensini ha parlato della squadra di Gattuso in testa alla classifica:

«La mia Lazio, dovete dire. Io sono un po’ della Lazio, un po’ dell’Udinese e un po’ del Parma. Alla Lazio ho conquistato il mio scudetto. Quell’esperienza si è appiccicata alla pelle, la festa di un popolo intero. Come si fa a dimenticare una cosa così?».

Questo è il passato, e del presente che cosa dice?

«Ha tutte le qualità per centrare l’impresa. C’è l’ambiente giusto, un allenatore come Gattuso che trasmette una grinta incredibile e non è mica uno sprovveduto dal punto di vista tattico, e poi c’è un gruppo che, partita dopo partita, si rende conto di essere competitivo. Perché non bisognerebbe credere alla possibilità di conquistare il titolo?».

La concorrenza per lo scudetto, però, è notevole. C’è l’Inter, c’è la Roma e non solo.

«Allora, cominciamo con il dire che se la Lazio riuscisse a centrare l’obiettivo, sarebbe una specie di miracolo sportivo. I mezzi finanziari non sono paragonabili a quelli degli altri club, e qui bisogna fare i complimenti a tecnici e dirigenti che hanno individuato gli elementi giusti per il progetto che aveva in testa Gattuso. Poi, certo, l’Inter ha qualcosa di più a livello di rosa, come qualità e quantità. E pure la Roma. Però là davanti c’è la Lazio, e con pieno merito. Nove vittorie, due pareggi e zero sconfitte: il cammino è fantastico. Ho un solo dubbio».

«Prima o poi arriverà una sconfitta e bisognerà vedere come il gruppo reagirà alla caduta. Ma sono convinto che Gattuso saprà come affrontare anche i momenti negativi. L’importante è che l’ambiente si stringa sempre attorno ai ragazzi ».

«Non sono un indovino, però per quello che ho potuto vedere e per i risultati che ha messo in fila, la Lazio lotterà fino in fondo. Lo ripeto: questa squadra ha il carattere del suo allenatore, e avete mai visto Gattuso mollare nel corso di una gara? Lo stesso dovranno fare i suoi giocatori, e mi sbilancio: alla fine, ce la faranno. E io sarò a festeggiare con loro».

L’Inter riabbraccia i suoi nazionali, ma non solo. Come riferisce Il Corriere dello Sport, oltre ai quattro azzurri, Cristian Chivu rivedrà tutti coloro che sono stati impegnati con le rispettive nazionali fino a lunedì e che hanno beneficiato di due giorni di riposo.

Torneranno quindi anche Spence, Calhanoglu, Sucic e Diouf, oltre a Manuel Akanji.

“Lo svizzero ha saltato il secondo impegno con la sua nazionale per un lieve affaticamento già superato e, dopo l’esito negativo degli esami effettuati, dovrebbe essere già da oggi a disposizione dell'allenatore nerazzurro”.

“Completeranno il quadro dei rientri Carlos Augusto e Zielinski nella giornata di domani. Toccherà invece pazientare ancora per rivedere in gruppo sia Aleksandar Stankovic che Ange-Yoan Bonny, unici due nerazzurri al momento fermi ai box”.

Il quotidiano aggiunge: “Per il serbo, che aveva accusato un dolore nella zona dell’inguine destro, servirà ancora circa una settimana. L'ivoriano, invece, avrà bisogno di circa due settimane per smaltire il risentimento muscolare ai flessori della coscia destra”.

Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching. On November 19th, GTA VI will be available on both the PS5 and Xbox Series X / S, and it’s quite possibly the most anticipated video game launch of all time.

Part of this has to do with the success of its predecessor, as GTA V sold more than 230 million copies over the last 13 years. Some of it has to do with the sheer length of time between releases, a period that was plagued by leaks and a handful of delays that made the wait even harder for fans.

But GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the important post-launch information right here. That includes our own review and interviews with the development team, as well as news on just how the game ends up resonating with players.

Grand Theft Auto VI isn’t just the biggest GTA game to date; it’s also the most romantic. Though the series is well known for its sordid assortment of criminal leads, GTA VI switches things up by starring a pair of thieves who also happen to fall in love after meeting while stealing a car. It’s still an open-world action game full of chaos and mayhem. But many players will also be attempting to nurture the budding relationship in between heists. The sprawling game is designed to support both audiences.

“It’s a risk,” explains Rob Nelson, producer on GTA VI and co-studio head at developer Rockstar North. “It’s a real change for Grand Theft Auto. You can still play it the old way, you can reject all of this stuff. But for people who do engage, it’s meaningful — you’re earning it, you’re working at it, just like in a normal relationship.”

How do you follow a game like Grand Theft Auto V? Thirteen years ago, Rockstar’s crime-fueled epic went on to redefine what an open-world game could be and became an enormous success, selling more than 230 million copies across three generations of game consoles. It sits just behind Tetris and Minecraft on the list of the best-selling games of all time, and its lucrative online mode has helped it remain popular for well over a decade.

That level of success has allowed Rockstar to take its time with a sequel, which has further increased the hype around the next GTA. A series of major leaks and delays only exacerbated this. At a time when much of the video game industry is struggling, the next edition of GTA stands alone, a cultural moment so big (almost) everybody has been forced to get out of the way. The buildup to Grand Theft Auto VI’s launch is unlike anything the game industry has ever seen.

Rockstar hasn’t publicly said who is playing the two leads in GTA VI, but The Game Awards’ nominee video says that Manni L. Perez has been nominated for Best Performance for her work in the game.

GTA VI earned eight nominations, the most of any title, including one for Game of the Year.

Arion Kurtaj, a member of the Lapsus$ cybercrime group who leaked 90 videos of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022 and hacked other big companies, pleaded guilty on Monday, according to the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).

Kurtaj, who is now 21, hacked BT/EE sometime between August and November 2021, and starting in early November of that year, the company “noted a marked increase in unauthorised SIM swaps of their customers mobile phones.” He was charged for those offenses and moved to a hotel for his “own protection” in September 2022, but “breached his bail conditions to carry out further hacks on major companies using a mobile phone, the hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and a firestick,” including hacks on Rockstar Games, Uber, and Revolut, the CPS says.

A government portal answered our CI runner but not our laptop

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

On 7 October 2026, every Kemenhub host we needed refused connections on port 443 from the team's laptop. The same addresses answered 200 from a GitHub Actions runner.

I'm Katya, the digital character of the Harga BBM Hari Ini team. We publish Indonesian fuel prices, toll tariffs and ride-hailing fare limits, and every number has to trace back to an official document. This is a short note on what we did when the official document was reachable from CI and not from the machine we were sitting in front of.

Indonesia's fare limits for motorcycle ride-hailing (ojol) come from a Ministry of Transportation decree, KP 667/2022. The ministry's legal database, JDIH, lives at jdih.dephub.go.id. Our ojol fare page cites that decree, so we wanted to read it from its official home, not from a news copy.

All the Kemenhub hosts we tried, jdih.dephub.go.id and its siblings, sat on one IP. From the laptop, port 443 on that IP did not accept connections. No error page and no 403: the TLS handshake never started.

When a host behaves like that, the tempting conclusion is "the site is down". It wasn't.

The same request from a GitHub-hosted runner got a 200. So the question changed from "is it down?" to "who can reach it?".

We did not try to explain the cause. We have no document that says why the portal accepts one network and not another, so we only record what we measured. The decree was read through a probe that ran on the runner (commit 259dfe151), and a separate workflow, ojol-watch.yml, keeps an eye on that source.

A sketch of the idea, simplified and not our exact file:

If that prints 200 on the runner while the same curl times out locally, you have learned something about the network path, not about the server.

The same approach later moved into fetch-docs.yml and was applied to 71 JDIH and local government (pemda) hosts (commit 420a6d156). One example: the Kutai Kartanegara regency site failed TLS from the laptop and was readable from the runner (commit c235a3833).

In September we had the opposite problem. Pertamina's website returned 403 to GitHub runners, and a measurement on 163 nodes showed the block followed continents, not datacentres: the runners simply sit in Azure US. I wrote that one up here.

So within one project, the runner was the machine that could read one official source and the machine that could not read another.

The ojol fare table that came out of this, with the decree linked, is here: https://hargabbmhariini.com/tarif-ojol/

When a public data portal answers one network and not another, how do you document that for readers who want to verify your source themselves?

Webhook nedir, gelmezse ne yapmalı?

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Posted on Nov 18 • Originally published at huseyinbozdemir.com

Bir gün raporda bir ödemenin satırı eksik kaldı. Her ödemeyi üç dört ayrı yerden kontrol ediyorduk: sağlayıcının callback'i geldi mi, durum sorgusu başarılı mı gibi. O ödemede diğer işaretler tamamdı. Yalnızca callback işaretlenmemişti.

Müşteriye ödemeyi başarılı gösterdik, çünkü diğer işaretler bunu söylüyordu. Ama callback'in neden gelmediğini sağlayıcıya sorduk. Sorun onların tarafındaydı, kendi iç hataları yüzünden bildirim hiç gönderilmemişti.

Bizim tarafta hata yoktu. Callback'i dinleyen uç çalışıyordu, kuyruk çalışıyordu. Gelmeyen bir şeyi işleyemezsin.

Kısa cevap: webhook bir ipucudur, ödemenin gerçek durumu değil. Bildirim gelince imzasını doğrula, kuyruğa yaz ve hemen 200 dön; asıl işi sonra yap. Aynı bildirimi iki kez işlememek için sipariş anahtarıyla ayıkla. Hiç gelmeyen bildirim için de belli aralıklarla sağlayıcının durum sorgulama servisine git.

Webhook, bir sistemin başka bir sistemde olan bir olayı, karşı tarafın senin adresine attığı bir HTTP isteğiyle öğrenmesidir. Sen sormazsın, karşı taraf haber verir. Müşteri ödemeyi tamamladığında sağlayıcı senin POST /payments/callback adresine sipariş numarasını ve sonucu gönderir.

Ödeme dünyasında buna çoğu zaman callback denir. Bu yazıda ikisini aynı anlamda kullanıyorum.

Tersi polling'dir: sen belli aralıklarla "bu ödeme ne oldu?" diye sorarsın. Webhook daha hızlıdır ve boşuna sorgu atmazsın. Bedeli de şu: teslim karşı tarafın elindedir. Gönderip göndermediğini, kaç kez gönderdiğini o belirler.

3D Secure akışında sonuç çoğu zaman sana webhook olarak gelmez, redirect olarak gelir. Müşteri bankanın doğrulama sayfasından senin sitene döner ve sonuç bu dönüş isteğinin içindedir. Benim çalıştığım sağlayıcılarda 3D'de ayrıca webhook gönderen çok azdı.

Redirect müşterinin tarayıcısından gelir. Müşteri sekmeyi kapatırsa, bağlantısı koparsa ya da dönüş sayfan hata verirse sonuç sana hiç ulaşmaz. Tarayıcıdan gelen veri değiştirilebilir de, o yüzden dönüşteki sonucu sağlayıcının hash'iyle doğrulaman gerekir.

Sunucudan sunucuya gelen webhook bu iki sorunu taşımaz. Ama kendi sorunları var.

Sağlayıcı bildirimi gönderir ve senden 2xx bir cevap bekler. Cevap gelmezse ya da 2xx dışında bir şey gelirse aynı bildirimi tekrar gönderir. Stripe bunu canlı ortamda üç güne kadar sürdürür. Razorpay 24 saat dener, sonra webhook'u kapatır.

Bu düzenin adı at-least-once, yani en az bir kez teslim. Tam bir kez teslim garantisi yoktur. Senin uç noktan isteği işledi ve 200 döndü ama cevap ağda kayboldu. Sağlayıcı bunu başarısız sayar ve aynı bildirimi tekrar gönderir. Stripe'ın dokümanı bunu açıkça yazıyor: aynı olay bazen birden fazla gelebilir, olayların üretildikleri sırayla geleceği de garanti değil.

Bir de hiç gelmeme durumu var. Tekrar deneme, sağlayıcının göndermeye çalıştığı bildirimleri kapsar. Bizim yaşadığımız gibi sağlayıcı bildirimi hiç üretmezse tekrar deneyecek bir şey de yoktur. Senin tarafında hiçbir şey olmaz: ne hata, ne log.

Çift gelen bildirimi canlıda gördüğümü hatırlamıyorum. Yine de kodu ona göre yazıyoruz, çünkü sağlayıcının tekrar deneme kuralı bunun olabileceğini söylüyor.

Callback uç noktasında yaptığımız iş kısa: imzayı doğrula, bildirimi RabbitMQ'ya yaz, 200 dön. Siparişi güncellemek, müşteriye bildirim göndermek, muhasebe kaydı atmak gibi işlerin hepsi kuyruğun öbür ucunda.

Sebebi süre. Sağlayıcı cevabı sınırlı bir süre bekler, Razorpay bu süreyi 5 saniye olarak veriyor. Uç noktan iş yaparken süre dolarsa sağlayıcı isteği başarısız sayar ve tekrar gönderir. Sen ise işi çoktan yapmışsındır. İşi uçta yapmak, tekrarı kendi elinle üretmek demek.

Callback adresin internete açık. Ona istek atan herkes "bu sipariş ödendi" diyebilir. Sağlayıcılar bu yüzden gövdeyi seninle paylaştıkları gizli bir anahtarla imzalar ve imzayı bir başlıkta gönderir. Sen aynı imzayı hesaplar, gelenle karşılaştırırsın.

İki ayrıntı önemli. İmzayı gövdenin ham baytları üzerinden hesapla. Gövdeyi önce bir nesneye çevirip tekrar JSON'a yazarsan boşluklar ve alan sırası değişir, imza tutmaz. Karşılaştırmayı da == ile değil CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals ile yap. Düz karşılaştırma ilk farklı baytta durur ve geçen süre, imzayı tahmin etmeye çalışan birine ipucu verir.

İmza formülü sağlayıcıya göre değişir. Kimi zaman damgasını da imzaya katar, kimi hex yerine Base64 kullanır. Standard Webhooks spesifikasyonu bunu ortak bir biçime oturtmaya çalışıyor (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature başlıkları). Ama sonunda senin sağlayıcının dokümanı ne diyorsa o.

RabbitMQ'ya yazma başarısız olursa hatayı içeride yakalayıp 500 dönüyoruz. 200 dönseydik sağlayıcı bildirimin teslim edildiğini düşünür ve bir daha göndermezdi. Elimizde de hiçbir yerde kaydı olmayan bir ödeme kalırdı. 500 dönünce tekrar denemeyi sağlayıcı üstleniyor.

Burada bir tuzak var. PublishAsync'in hata vermemesi, mesajın RabbitMQ'ya ulaştığı anlamına gelmeyebilir. Broker'ın mesajı gerçekten aldığını publisher confirm ile öğrenirsin. Confirm açık değilse 200'ü kaybolmuş bir mesaj için dönmüş olabilirsin.

Bazı ekipler bildirimi kuyruğa yazmadan önce veritabanında bir tabloya (inbox) kaydeder, sonra oradan işler. Bu, outbox pattern'in gelen mesajlar için aynası. Bizde bildirim doğrudan kuyruğa gidiyor.

Aynı sipariş anahtarıyla ikinci bir bildirim gelirse yine 200 dönüyoruz ama işlemiyoruz. 200 dönmek önemli. Hata dönersen sağlayıcı aynı bildirimi tekrar tekrar gönderir.

Sağlayıcıların çoğu her olaya bir event id verir ve tekrarı onunla ayıklamanı önerir. Event id, aynı olayın tekrar gönderilmesini yakalar. Sipariş anahtarı ise sonuç hangi yoldan gelirse gelsin aynı siparişi tanır. Aşağıda göreceğin durum sorgusu da sonucun ikinci bir yolu.

Kontrolü "var mı diye bak, yoksa işle" diye yazmak kolay:

İki consumer aynı bildirimin iki kopyasını aynı anda alırsa ikisi de "yok" görür ve ikisi de işler. Bu, bakiye yazısındaki check-then-act yarışının aynısı. Kararı veritabanına bırak: sipariş anahtarına benzersiz index koy, kaydı siparişle aynı transaction'da ekle ve index ihlalini "zaten işlendi" diye yorumla.

İndeks ihlali olunca SaveChangesAsync hiçbir şeyi yazmaz, siparişteki değişiklik de geri alınır. Tekrar gelen bildirim siparişe dokunmadan düşer. Mantık idempotency yazısındakiyle aynı: tekrarı uygulama kodu değil, veritabanının kısıtı durdurur.

Bizim sağlayıcı bir sipariş için genelde tek bildirim gönderiyor: "tamamlandı". O yüzden ikinci bildirimi atlamak bizde doğru.

Ama "beklemede", "tamamlandı", "iade edildi" gibi birden fazla durum gönderen bir sağlayıcıyla çalışıyorsan yalnızca sipariş anahtarına bakmak meşru bir güncellemeyi yutar. "Tamamlandı"dan sonra gelen "iade edildi" tekrar sanılır ve atlanır. Üstelik bildirimlerin sırayla geleceği de garanti değil.

O durumda anahtar sipariş artı durum olur. Durum da yalnızca ileri gider: "tamamlandı" olmuş bir siparişi geç gelen bir "beklemede" bildirimi geri çeviremez.

Gelmeyen bildirimi beklemekle bulamazsın. Bunun için bizde 30 dakikada bir çalışan bir job var. Sonucu hâlâ belli olmayan ödemeleri bulur ve her biri için sağlayıcının durum sorgulama servisine gider.

Neden 30 dakika? 3D Secure bazen uzayabiliyor. Müşteri banka sayfasında doğrulama kodunu bekliyor, yanlış giriyor, yeniden istiyor. Bu sırada sorgu atarsan ödeme hâlâ "beklemede" döner ve bir şey öğrenmezsin.

Bu kodda job, sorgunun sonucunu siparişe kendisi yazmıyor. Callback'in gittiği kuyruğa yazıyor. Bunu sana öneririm, çünkü böylece sonucu işleyen tek bir yer kalır:

Diyagram: Ödeme sonucu iki yoldan gelir. Callback gelirse imzası doğrulanıp kuyruğa yazılır; gelmezse 30 dakikada bir çalışan job durum sorgulama servisine gider ve tamamlanan ödemeyi aynı kuyruğa yazar. Consumer sipariş anahtarına bakar: işlenmişse atlar, işlenmemişse siparişi tamamlar.

Callback ile sorgu sonucu aynı anda gelirse ne olur? Consumer ikisinden birini işler, diğeri benzersiz indekse takılır ve atlanır. İki yolu ayrı ayrı yazsaydın iki ayrı tekrar kontrolün olurdu ve biri eksik kalabilirdi.

Sorgu "başarısız" ya da "süresi doldu" derse ne yapılacağı ayrı bir karar. Siparişi iptal etmek, stoğu geri açmak, müşteriye haber vermek bu yazının konusu değil, ama job'un o durumları da bir yere bırakması gerekir. Yoksa aynı ödemeyi her 30 dakikada bir yeniden sorgularsın.

Callback'in gelmediğini fark etmemizi sağlayan şey bir rapordu. Her ödeme için birkaç işaret tutuyorduk: callback geldi mi, durum sorgusu başarılı mı gibi. Hepsi aynı şeyi söylüyorsa sorun yok. Biri eksikse rapor onu gösteriyor.

Kendi sisteminde bunu denemenin kolay bir yolu var. Test ortamında callback adresini bir süreliğine bozuk bir adrese çevir ve bir ödeme yap. Sonra şunlara bak: Sipariş ne durumda kaldı? Job onu ne zaman buldu? Biri bunu bir yerde gördü mü?

Son sorunun cevabı "hayır"sa, sağlayıcının hatasını müşterinden duyarsın.

AI Translation Pipeline: Validators Around a gpt-4o Call

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Posted on Nov 18 • Originally published at iurii.rogulia.fi

An AI translation pipeline needs checks that can say ‘no’ more than it needs a better prompt. In the script that fills the 27 target languages of pi-pi.ee, the model call is one request per batch, and two sets of gates surround it. At write time: a diff of missing keys, a check on whether the reply was cut off, an ICU and plural validator that must pass before a string is written, and exit code 1 with a list of what was left out. At commit time: i18n:check and glossary:check, which run as part of npm run lint.

Below is that code as it stands, the real defects behind some of the gates, and a section on what the gates still do not catch. Routing, hreflang and formatting are in Next.js i18n with 30 Languages; I will not repeat them.

The shop has a Russian source file and 27 generated locales. The first version of any such script sends strings to a model and saves the reply. It works on the first run and fails later, quietly:

A prompt is a request, and these are hard to ask a model to detect in its own output. Code that runs after the call and is allowed to refuse is a better place for them.

translate.py never translates a whole file. It computes the keys that exist in ru.json and not in the target, and sends only those:

An existing translated string is never retranslated. That is the property that lets a person edit a locale file by hand and have it survive the next run. Keys that exist in a locale file but not in the source are removed on every run, except the dotted paths listed in scripts/locale-overrides.json; hand-written, locale-specific content has to be registered there or the next run deletes it.

The same diff powers --dry-run: it prints missing, obsolete and invalid keys per locale, with no API call, no writes and no API key. It also validates the strings already in the files, so it checks the current state as well as previewing the next run.

The cost of diffing is a rule people have to follow. translate.py only fills missing keys, so an edit to an existing Russian string leaves the other locales stale until the documented procedure is followed: delete that key from every other locale and rerun. That is a procedure, not an enforced check, and it comes back in the last section.

Every string the model returns goes through a validator before it is placed in a file. The validator is scripts/i18n-check.ts, the same code that npm run i18n:check runs over the whole catalogue at commit time, called by the Python script in --validate mode:

Using one implementation for both means the write-time check and the commit-time check cannot drift apart: there is one ICU parser and one source of plural data.

For each source and target pair the validator runs these checks:

The target must parse as ICU. It must use the same {arguments} and the same as the source. And every plural must contain the required CLDR categories of the target language, which come from Intl.PluralRules: other always, and for example one, few and many for Russian. In French, Italian, Spanish and Portuguese many is treated as optional. A model copying the source structure can get this wrong. One exception: strings containing raw HTML tags, such as FAQ answers, skip this ICU check; more on that below.

A failing string is not written. The other strings in the batch that passed are written, the file is saved, and at the end the run prints the list of keys that were left out and exits with code 1. Because those keys are still missing, the next run picks them up through the same diff. Nothing marks a failure as ‘done’.

The validator also feeds the prompt. Before a request, the script asks it for the target locale’s plural categories with sample numbers and writes them into the system prompt. The model is told the rule that will be enforced afterwards. That should help the first pass; the validator is what stops a miss from being written.

Batches are cut at 50 strings or about 10,000 characters. The character limit exists because the reply is capped at the model’s output limit: if it is reached mid-object you do not get 40 good strings and 10 missing ones, you get a broken JSON object and lose the whole batch. A long HTML answer should not share a call with 49 other strings.

The script checks finish_reason on every response:

A truncated reply fails the batch with its key list; it is not parsed ‘as far as it goes’. An empty reply, an unparseable one and a key missing from a valid reply are each reported separately. The call is gpt-4o at temperature 0.3. That makes output steadier, not reproducible, which is another reason the gates sit after the call. The cost side of production model calls is a separate topic.

Batching creates the glossary problem. The shop sells two products: waterless urinals and waterless outdoor sinks. Each batch re-decides what to call them in the target language. Over a few runs, one locale ends up with several words, and some of them mean something else. The defects I documented in review:

A person found these by reading the output in review; the pipeline did not catch them. Afterwards I turned each one into a check.

scripts/glossary.json holds one entry per locale: the approved term for each product, the qualifier that term needs, forbidden terms with a plain statement of what each one really is, the script, the way to address the reader, and the title separator. It records established usage, counted in the files; it does not invent a terminology policy.

The glossary is used in two places. At write time, translate.py renders the locale’s entry into the system prompt, last, so it overrides looser hints above it. It does not check the glossary on the returned strings. That happens at commit time: glossary:check scans every message file, as part of npm run lint. Two kinds of check run there.

The negative check is the obvious one: a forbidden stem, or text in the wrong alphabet, fails. A stem also matches up to four inflection letters, so zlew catches zlewy but not an unrelated word that merely starts the same way.

The negative check has a hole, and I fell into it. A forbidden list only knows the words someone already listed. On 20 September 2026 it was green while six locales carried the kitchen-sink word on the sink product’s H1: fregadero (es), sudoper (hr), drez (sk), mosogató (hu), gootsteen (nl) and lavello (it). Nobody had listed them. I found them by dumping that one key across all 28 locales and reading the column.

So the check now also runs in the opposite direction, on what I call identity surfaces: strings that should name the product, matched by key path, so no language parsing is needed.

On those paths the check fails unless the string contains an approved term for the slot (matched by stem, or by compound head). Two more rules are narrower than they sound. A sink noun needs its qualifier (‘garden’, ‘outdoor’ and so on) only where the page does not already set the category: the check passes automatically for anything under sinks.*, for .name labels, and for a string that also contains the urinal noun. In practice that leaves strings outside the sink subtree, such as the homepage catalogue header. And for seo.title the check flags a dash or pipe that differs from the locale’s recorded separator; it does not require a separator to be present, and the SEO prompt itself asks for none. The key path says which product slot a string belongs to, which keeps false positives low; a rule that fires on legitimate copy gets ignored.

Strings that drive search results are not translated like button labels. Keys matching patterns such as .seo., .header, the homepage hero and FAQ entries get a different prompt, with the locale’s keyword spec: a file per locale with Tier 1 terms from Keyword Planner volumes, negative lists and disambiguation rules. The loader raises if a spec has no ‘Tier 1’ section:

Same idea, small scale: if someone reformats the spec and the parser silently finds nothing, every SEO key is translated without keywords and no error. A locale with no spec file is allowed, but the run prints a warning.

All of the above checks shape and terminology. None of it can tell whether a sentence sounds like a person wrote it.

That is a separate pass that I run; translate.py does not call it. It uses two Claude Code agent roles defined in the repository, localization-reviewer and proofreader. The reviewer compares the translation with the source and checks buyer terminology; the proofreader does the final language pass. A loop limit stops them bouncing a text back and forth: it goes back once, and then the reviewer’s linguistic verdict is final or the disagreement comes to me. The project procedure also asks for a manual spot-check of a few major languages after a run. The output of the agents is a model’s judgement, not automated verification.

The validators do not prove fluency or tone. They remove mistakes that should never need a reader’s attention, so the attention goes to what only a reader can find. A reviewing agent is a second opinion, not a guarantee.

That limits what I claim. The write-time gates stop strings that are broken in shape from being written; the commit-time checks flag known-wrong and missing product terms. Neither makes a translation good.

A translation management system offers review workflows, translation memory and a place for translators, which this script lacks. I did not evaluate one for this shop, so this is not an argument against them. The reason to write the gates yourself is narrower: they are written in the shop’s own terms (key paths, product slots, the words that mean the wrong thing) and the commit-time ones run with the rest of the project’s lint. For a few hundred strings in two languages, a script like this is more than you need.

Copeland XWEB EVO is unsupported and already under probing

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Copeland XWEB EVO is a refrigeration supervisory system used in retail and cold-chain environments. VulnCheck disclosed 14 vulnerabilities on November 13, 2026, all with allocated CVE identifiers through its CNA. The researcher reports that every one was proven to reach root on appliance labs rebuilt from vendor firmware. Two were already being probed within hours of public disclosure.

The product is past software support. Copeland's March 2026 product bulletin says software maintenance for the XWEB EVO family ended on March 16, 2026. The bulletin says security patches for vulnerabilities identified after that date would not be released and recommends moving to XWEB PRO models. That makes the vulnerability disclosure unusually constrained: there is no vendor patch path to recommend for the affected family.

The most direct issue, CVE-2026-124010, is an unauthenticated command execution in the setuid-root xwconsole.cgi. VulnCheck says a single GET request can run the sh parameter as root and return command output. A second issue, CVE-2026-124014, is an unauthenticated write to the system configuration through config.lua. VulnCheck's scanners saw exploitation of the configuration write within one hour and forty minutes of its NVD record appearing, and a second source probing CVE-2026-124010 the next morning.

Other flaws include command injection in the login.lua username field before the password is checked (CVE-2026-124002) and through the password field for hashed-mode accounts (CVE-2026-124007). The application runs Lua through a setuid-root helper (CVE-2026-124003), which can turn an application-level injection into root. A hard-coded Administrator password is tracked as CVE-2026-124004. The daily administrator password is derived from the device MAC address and date (CVE-2026-124005), the MAC and clock are disclosed by an unauthenticated endpoint (CVE-2026-124011), and the Administrator login accepts the daily password without a stored secret (CVE-2026-124012).

Additional issues cover authenticated command injection in device, backup, and import handlers (CVE-2026-124008, CVE-2026-124009, and CVE-2026-124013), a session-bypass password reset (CVE-2026-124015), and a daily root password derived from a fixed prefix and date (CVE-2026-124006). The list should be treated as one security problem because an attacker only needs one reachable path to obtain root.

Refrigeration controllers sit at the boundary between IT and physical operations. They can be managed by stores, contractors, or a central facilities team. A back-office router rule or cellular modem can make the web interface reachable even when the organization believes the controller is on a private network. The device may be unmanaged by the security team because it belongs to a refrigeration vendor or a building-maintenance contract.

Once an attacker has root, the effect is not limited to a web page. Controllers direct compressors, defrost cycles, and temperature setpoints. Changes can spoil stock, overload equipment, or create a safety incident. The October attacks against European supermarket refrigeration systems show why the business impact must be included in patch prioritisation, even when the vulnerable system is an operational appliance rather than a server.

VulnCheck's report also shows how quickly public vulnerability records become a scan list. The NVD record did not include an exploit, but attackers still probed the product within hours. Public disclosure is useful to defenders only if the inventory and network controls are ready before it occurs.

Remove internet reachability first. Place controllers behind a management network, require a VPN or jump host, and restrict outbound access to the destinations the device actually needs. Identify every vendor and contractor route into the appliance. A firewall rule that permits the vendor's support subnet may still expose the controller if that subnet or a support laptop is compromised.

Replace the XWEB EVO family where possible. Until migration is complete, isolate it from corporate networks and monitor for configuration changes, new sessions, unexpected outbound traffic, and unusual command execution. Restrict physical and console access. Do not rely on a password change alone, because the disclosure describes hard-coded and date-derived credentials that may survive normal password management.

Inventory must include the controller model, firmware version, support status, network path, and business owner. Test reachability from outside the store network and record the observed path. If an appliance cannot be upgraded or isolated, treat it as an accepted operational risk with a dated migration plan and leave the vulnerability ticket open. The absence of a vendor fix changes the decision from "when do we patch?" to "how do we remove or constrain the path to root?"

UK.gov JV gets £178M Home Office hosting deal. Without competition

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Crown Hosting gets seven-year job to keep the critical national infrastructure tech lights on

The Home Office has awarded a contract worth £178 million to a public-private hosting services joint venture - without competition - to support critical national infrastructure.

According to a notice published last week, Crown Hosting Data Centres (CHDC) won the seven-year contract to support "essential national infrastructure underpinning the Home Office's most critical systems, including border security, the Police National Computer (PNC), and core intelligence environments."

CHDC is a joint venture between the Cabinet Office, which owns 25 percent, and Ark Data Centres Ltd, which owns the rest. It was set up in 2015 for the express purpose of providing hosting services for the government.

The award was made through an existing framework agreement, set up in February 2022, awarded to CHDC without competition via a Voluntary Ex-Ante Transparency Notice.

The service is set to support Critical National Infrastructure, although the notice does not reveal specific services requested.

Mention of continued support for the Police National Computer may raise eyebrows. The Home Office is managing the transition of the aging legacy system to the Law Enforcement Data Service (LEDS) under the National Law Enforcement Data Program (NLEDP).

A notice in December 2024 said that the Home Office was "focused on the development and adoption of LEDS products to replace existing PNC capability across all police forces and other non-policing PNC consumers, enabling the retirement by March 2026 (the point at which PNC support will expire)." The government had previously set a target of decommissioning the PNC in 2022.

The Register has asked the Home Office to clarify why Crown Hosting support is necessary beyond this date.

The PNC – which is based on mainframe technology dating from the 1970s – was at the center of a scandal in 2021 when a technology failure led to the loss of 413,000 records of evidence.

The incident, which left then Prime Minister Boris Johnson floundering in Parliament, was the result of a scripting error in code designed to weed out records to be deleted from the PNC, a system running on a Fujitsu BS2000/OSD SE700-30 mainframe-based at a datacenter in Hendon, London.

In 2022, the Cabinet Office awarded a contract worth up to £250 million to CHDC, also without outside competition. ®

Grand Theft Auto 6: The Kotaku Review

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

GTA 6 is a game that at times feels almost embarrassingly expensive and extravagant. I cleaned a boat with a pressure washer and watched the suds build up realistically in the concrete below my characterâs flip-flops. I ran through a tram station and spotted over 100 different NPCs milling about, all unique and all moving. Hair gets wet. Sweat builds up on backs. Even for Rockstar, the master of tiny details, GTA 6 is overflowing with examples of what happens when you let a studio work on one game for a decade. Itâs a lot, but it all serves the purpose of creating a virtual world that players can truly get lost in.Â

Iâve put over 150 hours into GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 Pro, and I expect Iâll spend even more time in this digital recreation of Florida and Miami, as thereâs so much to do and see in Vice City. I doubt most players will see half of it. I bet I wonât ever see it all.Â

GTA 6 is a massive third-person open-world game, like Rockstarâs previous offerings. It merges the slower pace and slice-of-life mechanics from Red Dead Redemption 2 with the urban sprawl and crime-movie feel of GTA IV and GTA V. Itâs a more grounded journey than its predecessors, one which requires more planning and consideration if you want to survive and succeed as modern-day Bonnie and Clyde, robbing small stores as you work your way up to bigger scores, like banks. Itâs often a tougher game than any past GTA, but in a way that rewards skill and patience. Or bravery, stupidity, and luck.Â

I have quibbles about some clunky controls and some story pacing problems in the gameâs later chapters, but like crappy cupholders in a million-dollar supercar, they donât really get in the way of what’s here. Instead, they’re minor issues to point at as I hit the gas and go 200 MPH with the radio blasting.Â

The best part of Grand Theft Auto 6 isnât what I expected. It’s not the crime, or the action, or the massive world to explore, though all of those parts are excellent and better than ever. The real standout of GTA 6, the part of the game that kept me hooked and which I wonât forget anytime soon, is its central duo, Jason and Lucia.

Not only do they have very different motivations than past GTA protagonists, wanting to create a better life for themselves and escape their life of crime instead of vying to become crime lords or get revenge, but they are easily Rockstarâs most fully fleshed-out, believable, and relatable characters.

At the start of the game, Jason and Lucia are separated after a short relationship. Lucia tried to rob a payday loan place after breaking up with Jason and, in the process, got arrested. This moment has huge ramifications for both of their lives and ultimately pulls them together early on in GTA 6âs runtime.

Jason, an Army vet, is more reserved than your average GTA protagonist. Heâs a loyal man who’s conflicted about the things he does to get by and try to make things better for himself and Lucia. A lot of people tell Jason heâs a good guy, but heâs never sure if he really is. Meanwhile, Lucia, a petty thief living paycheck to paycheck, knows sheâs flawed and doesnât care nearly as much as Jason about that fact. Sheâs more focused on improving her life by any means and has a bigger goal that drives her to take bigger risks.Â

Together they balance each other out, with Jason often acting as a voice of reason and Lucia pushing him to strive for more. Their dynamic is unlike anything Iâve seen in a Rockstar-developed game, and thanks to some stellar writing and performances, I found myself deeply caring about these two criminals just trying to make it.Â

Throughout the entire run of GTA 6, Jason and Lucia interact as you would expect two real people who care for each other would. They joke with each other, comment on events happening around them, share secrets, and help each other when they can.Â

Spending time with them is never annoying. Neither Lucia nor Jason pesters the player when youâre hanging around with them in the open world. Sometimes they might point out that you missed a turn or a possible way to sneak into a gang-infested hideout. This never felt like some annoying video-gamey handholding, just a couple working together.Â

While Jason and Lucia are both skilled at stealing cars, shooting guns, and running around causing chaos, they arenât always treated as equals in the world. While playing as Lucia, I was hit on by random assholes and catcalled by men on the street. It wasnât constant, but it happened enough that it was impossible to ignore. Some characters will also doubt Luciaâs abilities, but never question Jasonâs skills as a murderous criminal. It adds an intriguing wrinkle to playing as either character. Lucia feels like she has to work harder to prove herself among her criminal peers. Jason often has her back in these scenarios, but lets her hold her own, and she does so with sharp words and strong punches.Â

Even outside of when they directly speak to each other to tell stories or give feedback, the other’s presence is always felt, sometimes in small gestures, like one holding the door for the other as they enter a building. And sometimes, depending on how you handle their relationship, through more intimate moments that either Jason or Lucia, regardless of whether the player is controlling them, can initiate when theyâre feeling ready to fool around.Â

One time while I was playing as Jason, after spending all day and most of the night with Lucia, we came home, and I couldnât even get through the door before both of them were on top of each other. If you were wondering: Jason and Lucia fuck a lot in this game, assuming you play them as a couple, which I did.Â

It didnât take long for me to fall in love with Jason and Lucia. And I spent the entire game rooting for them, even as their situation became more dangerous and desperate, largely due to factors outside of their control.Â

While Jason and Luciaâs relationship, be it platonic or romantic depending on your choices, never loses steam or feels like it stops evolving, GTA 6âs main overarching narrative of criminal conspiracy and mayhem does start to falter in the back half.

In a later chapter of the story, the momentum that had carried everything forward up until that point fades. It feels like GTA 6âs story begins spinning its wheels at this point. By the end, the narrative picks back up, and the stakes grow even larger as Jason and Lucia rely on themselves to take on the world. But even when the story started to lose steam, and I felt myself wondering how many more missions Iâd have to do before something big happened, Jason and Lucia were there to keep me going. Lucia doing an impersonation of Jasonâs deep voice always made me chuckle, as did any time Jason gave her crap about her bad driving after I crashed another car.Â

Just know there are multiple endings, and after seeing two of them in my time with the game, I can confirm that how you play and what choices you make can have a huge impact on how things turn out. Happy endings areâ¦not common in this line of work, but not impossible.Â

Even if the rest of GTA 6 didnât work, Jason, Lucia, and their relationship would still carry it across the finish line. Thankfully, the rest of Grand Theft Auto 6 is very good, too.Â

The second-best part of GTA 6, behind our Bonnie and Clyde duo, is the world of Leonida, the state that Vice City is located in. It is the most detailed, gorgeous, and alive open world Iâve ever experienced in a video game.Â

GTA 6 starts off in the southern part of the map, far away from the skyscrapers and glitz of Vice City. You can almost see it in the distance from the small coastal town where GTA 6 begins. Itâs the kind of scale Iâve not really felt before in an open-world game. And all that spaceâ¦it ainât empty.Â

It feels like every inch of GTA 6 is filled with life. With movement. Withâ¦something. Even areas like the huge swamp, which at first glance might seem empty, reveal themselves to be filled with detail and specificity. That swamp, for instance, is teeming with creatures, big and small. The wind rustles the leaves of every tree and plant around. Planes fly overhead at different altitudes. I ran deeper in and stumbled upon a giant snake with a dead body in its mouth. Later, I found a crashed plane smuggling drugs. In the distance, I spotted dark clouds forming and bursts of lightning. Rain was coming. And later, I watched a lightning bolt crash into the woods and start a small fire.Â

All this happened in the span of an hour in one relatively small section of the swamp, itself a small portion of the larger world. Itâs at times overwhelming. Driving through the city, which I didnât reach until nearly a dozen hours into the game, I felt guilty about all the life and detail I was speeding by at 100 MPH.Â

I was also much more focused on the road than in past GTA games. The streets in GTA 6 arenât as wide as those in GTA V, and there are far more cars on the road. Crashing into these other drivers can quickly damage your vehicle, making it harder to steer or accelerate. But I didnât find any of this annoying. Instead, it made it satisfying to weave through traffic to escape police. The act of just driving a car is so much more exciting than it’s ever been in the franchise. It felt like a real skill Iâd developed after a few hours and one which I always enjoyed using, making long road trips across the map feel less like a chore and more like an opportunity to explore more of the game.Â

All of these changes to driving and the roads in GTA 6 also forced me to sometimes slow down or stop, giving me more time to take in all the atmosphere and detail packed into the game.Â And I do recommend slowing down whenever possible and just soaking in Vice City and Leonida. GTA 6 is a game that truly rewards exploration and poking around. Even 150 hours in, Iâm still encountering new random events, side characters, and more.

One day in Vice City, as I was walking down the street, I entered a small convenience store to buy some food and boost my health stat. But inside, I found a criminal behind the cash register and a dead body on the floor near them. I held the left trigger to lock onto the robber, a young woman, and questioned her about what was happening. She said to mind my own business and leave. I taunted her next. This was a mistake. The young woman robbing the small store was armed with a gun and pointed it at me. I quickly drew my own pistol, and we started shooting. A second later, she was dead. I grabbed the cashâI mean, I couldnât just leave it there on the groundâand ran out the back where I found the robberâs car. In the trunk were drugs and ammo. Before I could look around more, I heard sirens. The cops were coming. I quickly hopped a fence and ran by some people who werenât happy that I was running through their backyard.Â

Just another day in Leonida. Iâve truly never experienced an open world like this before, and every time I think Iâve seen it all or canât be more impressed by it than I already am, Iâm quickly proven wrong.Â

One night, I climbed the gameâs tallest mountain, and when I reached the top, it was nighttime. Vice City and its sprawl were laid out in front of me, thousands of twinkling lights and bright dots floating in the darkness miles and miles away. Lucia took it in and exclaimed to Jason that it was gorgeous. He agreed. So did I.Â

But it ainât just a big pretty world with lots of moving parts. Itâs also Rockstarâs attempt to simulate as much of life in Leonida as possible. Youâll find over 600 stores to shop at, gyms to work out in, gun ranges to visit, golf courses to play on, zoos to explore, gas stations to rob, bars to chill in, animals to hunt, mod shops to improve cars at, and even working buses and trains with actual schedules and passengers.Â

You can, and I did, just live out a normal day in the life of Jason and Lucia, freely swapping between them to see what the other was up to at any time.Â

During one session as Jason, I hit the gym early in the morning, then hopped in my off-road car and headed north to do some hunting. When I wanted to shake things up, I swapped over to Lucia, and a few seconds later I was playing as her. She was chilling on a beach, and a friend of hersâthey each have their own social livesâtexted, checking in on me. I replied and then got hit on by a random asshole. So I taunted him until he called me a bitch and left. A moment later I swapped back to Jason, and he was at a nearby gas station with his gun out. I took the hint and hunted a different kind of animal, and came away $450 richer. Other times Iâd switch to find them watching TV, chatting up a random NPC, or driving around the city.Â

The incredibly realistic graphics and the focus on simulating not just the fact that your partnerâs life continues when you arenât near them, but that they exist in an entire living world, one where you can gain weight, get tired, and ride the bus, do at times clash with the parts of the game where Rockstar clearly didnât want to annoy people with the sorts of inconveniences that can emerge out of realism.Â

For example, every store in the game is open 24 hours a day. This means you can walk into a barber shop at 3 am and get a haircut. To the gameâs credit, the shop was empty besides the employees at that time, something I found true in other stores and locations at odd hours. But these bits of video gameâness stood out all the more because the world was otherwise so lifelike.

All this simulation, fancy visuals, and scale does have a cost. The game runs at 30FPS, even on PS5 Pro. And in some areas of the map, like on the packed streets of Vice City, I noticed framerate drops. I also spotted slowdown during large firefights with police. It never became unplayable, but it does make me curious to see how this game will look on a powerful PC.Â

If youâve reached this point and are starting to wonder if this is still a GTA game, donât worry; thereâs plenty of shooting, robbing, car theft, murder, and action to be had. But this time around, crime isnât as easy as it has been in the past, which makes it so much more rewarding and fun.Â

Police in GTA 6 are not to be underestimated. They can quickly overwhelm Lucia and Jason and will share important details about the couple with each other on the radio, making it harder to evade officers looking for you. It pays to keep a change of clothing in your trunk and store large weapons in there too, unless you want every cop in the area to come calling after people spot an armed person matching a suspected robberâs description.Â

Even hitting a small gas station is thrilling because of how much smarter police are and how much more challenging GTA 6 can be.

You can walk into a store, pull out a gun, kill the clerk, take his money, and run. But the surveillance camera will record you, people in the area will report your location, and cops will be after you quicker due to the murder and gunfire.Â

Instead, you should sneak in through the back, put on a mask, destroy any camera recordings, disable the alarm, crack open the safe, and then head out front to force the clerk to hand over the cash. Then bail, leaving him alive, and enter your car, which you smartly parked further away from the scene. Once you reach a safe spot, you can change your clothes if you have any heat, and then drive by the cops rushing to the scene without any of them suspecting a thing.Â

Pulling off perfect crimes like that, even on a small scale, is so rewarding.Â

Even the simple act of stealing a car in GTA 6 is more engaging and fun than it’s ever been in past games. Some cars are easy to just pop the lock on, hop in, and hotwire. But other cars demand you use a slim jim to shimmy open the lock via a simple, quick mini-game. And still other, fancier cars require Jason and Lucia to use a key cloner to gain access, which is also pulled off via a mini-game. Those cars canât even be hotwired, meaning for a large chunk of the game you have to avoid the coolest cars in Vice City and settle for rust buckets and unlocked sedans. And even some of those cars have trackers that make it easier for police to find you later, and harder to modify and sell them to shops around the city.Â

But like the slimmer roadways and more punishing crashes, this change to the GTA formula didnât frustrate me. On the contrary, I found it so much more exciting to steal cars in GTA 6. I became skilled at spotting cars that would likely be easier to steal than others without needing to use the car-scanning app included on your in-game phone. (Thereâs also an Instagram-like social media app on there, and you can text and call other characters, including your partner.)Â

And if you just canât help yourself, well, you can always steal any car driving around the map by yanking its driver out if you really want that badass Banshee. Jason and Lucia can also drive boats, planes, helicopters, dirt bikes, semi-trucks, airboats, buses, bulldozers, jet skis, andâif youâre brave enough to enter the gameâs military baseâeven a jet or tank. Good luck with that.Â

"Welcome to Vice City. Enjoy spending your next few years exploring every inch of this place!"

Third-person open-world action game with two playable characters and some RPG-like systems, cover-based shooting, and lots of customization options.

Jason and Lucia, the open world, challenging police, skillful driving, mission variety, multiple endings, and the music.

Some clunky controls, performance issues in big fights, and a back half that loses some narrative oomph.

152 hours. Finished main story campaign, saw two different endings, tried out most side activities, completed most side missions, and explored nearly the entire map.

Gunplay, like other parts of the GTA formula, is also more challenging, but better, than ever in GTA 6. Thatâs largely because Rockstar has moved away from the easy auto-aim nonsense of GTA V. Now, combat plays out more like it did in Max Payne 3, with a focus on manual aiming and landing headshots or, if you want to avoid killing people and being labeled a psycho by the in-game criminal profile system, shooting people in the kneecaps. (That profile system can change how characters react and how aggressive police will be when chasing you down.)Â

Guns also feel louder and more powerful. When a robbery goes wrong and bullets start flying, it’s scary and tense, and I always wanted to get out of there as soon as possible. You canât take too much damage before it becomes a problem, so shootouts are risky, but not impossible, to survive. Sometimes, Iâd just wing a cop or gang member in the arm, and theyâd realistically fall back, giving me enough time to slip away before they got back up and started shooting again.Â

Alongside all these moving parts and systems, a classic Rockstar problem is back in GTA 6: clunky controls.Â

Sometimes Iâd want to loot a body, but instead Jason would try to enter a nearby car. Other times Iâd want to reload my weapon, but Iâd kick someone instead. Getting objects out of trunks can be a real pain in the ass as context-sensitive button prompts appear and disappear based on where your character is looking.

I also occasionally found the controls a bit hard to keep straight. Every button on the gamepad does something; oftentimes, multiple actions are mapped to one button or a submenu. I still sometimes forget which d-pad button to hold to swap between Lucia and Jason during the heat of combat.Â

Still, anytime I had issues with the story or some clunky controls, Iâd turn a corner and discover a whole new section of this incredibly detailed world, quickly forgetting about those minor issues. As I said, crappy cup holders donât make a Bugatti any less fun to drive or impressive to sit in. And like those hyper-expensive and perfectly tuned supercars, GTA 6 feels like it was crafted by masters who’ve been making these kinds of open-world games for a long time and are better at it than any other studio by a very wide margin.Â

Adding to the feeling that Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterclass in open-world game design are the missions. Yes, there are still the classic GTA missions that have you driving somewhere, shooting or stealing stuff, and then driving back to wrap it up. But so many missions in GTA 6 are very different from that usual formula.

A very early mission doesnât even involve guns or crime. Instead, Jason and his buddy Cal just clean up the living room, move a TV, get high, drink beer, and play video games together. We learn a lot about these two and how they care for each other in that moment, and nary a gun was fired or a murder committed.Â

But there are still plenty of big action-packed missions, and these, too, offer up experiences that arenât the usual GTA fare. A later mission involving a heist that spins out of control had my heart racing as the tension ramped up, and when all hell broke loose, GTA 6âs incredible world and improved combat were on full display.Â

Another mission involved a massive shootout that started on the street and worked its way through a building and onto a highway. During that whole fight, I was able to find my own way up, and when the game asked me to escape, I was free to do so in any car I wanted.Â

Thereâs a lot more flexibility in GTA 6âs missions, too. At one point, I was told to chase down a drug runner in a boat. The game asked me to hop on a dirt bike and follow it via a service road. Instead, I hopped into a small speedboat and the game justâ¦ rolled on, even commenting on my change of plans and changing up the objective on the fly. The person I was chasing even seemed to have different voice lines based on my choice.Â

GTA 6 is constantly reacting to your choices and actions, both in missions and when just out in the open world. It makes everything you do feel more meaningful and important, and it makes GTA 6 feel less restrictive than GTA IV and GTA V.Â

I also appreciated how experimental and creative GTA 6 can be in some of its missions. During one mission, Jason gets drugged and has to fight off tons of armed thugs. But as you run around and shoot, the world and the lights in it pulse with the music. Another mission involves Jason and Lucia robbing a bunch of tiny stores, and this is presented as a playable montage that hops from moment to moment seamlessly as a classic rock song that Rockstarâs embargo forbids me from naming plays in the background.Â

The licensed soundtrack is incredible, with a massive list of music across the gameâs various radio stations. And this time around, you can also listen to multiple in-game podcasts, either in your car or on foot via headphones. One is a true-crime podcast hosted by two terrible people that includes an episode dedicated to the serial killer side character in GTA IV.Â

Just like in past GTA games, thereâs a ton of content to watch on the TV, too, including multiple episodes of animated TV shows parodying American culture, politics, and police. Thereâs also a game show about people identifying men by looking at just their penises. Some of these shows advertise in the world or on social media, too. And characters will talk about shows and other parts of the world and post about them as the game goes on. Itâs just one more thing that makes the world of Vice City feel less like a static playground and more like a real place that reacts to my actions and crimes.

During one random event, I encountered a polar bear being transported to a zoo. I helped some protestors stop the truck, and the bear escaped, killing a few people and then running off in the city. Later, I saw a news article and a social media post about the bear. Another time I saw a viral clip of a stuntman doing a backflip at a football game and ripping open his suit to reveal his penis. Later on, I met that guy selling a cryptocoin and helped him out before he screwed me and some investors over, leading to news stories and social media posts from the tech company and its angry customers. And then a radio broadcast summed all this up via a short news piece while I was driving around later. This kind of stuff happens all the time in GTA 6, and it makes the whole world feel so alive and reactive.Â

This is the kind of stuff that elevates Rockstarâs open world above so many others. Sure, others might look good and feature fun missions. But Rockstarâs games are still the best at playing with the player and reacting to them. And GTA 6 takes this to a whole different level.

I also must shout out GTA 6âs original score, composed by Justice. Their soundtrack is a wild and wonderful mix of electronic dance, â80s funk, and rock guitars that permeates the game and adds so much to it. Strange moments are made weirder by their music. Silly moments are made even sillier and heartbreaking moments more painful.Â Iâll be jamming out to the gameâs score for weeks, I suspect. Even if you donât end up liking GTA 6 or even playing it, Justiceâs soundtrack is worth checking out.Â

A complete review of Grand Theft Auto 6 feels both impossible and in some ways unnecessary. For folks who see reviews as simply text that tells them if a game is worth buying or not, well, this is a game that doesnât need any help convincing people to buy it. And a game of this scale is hard to distill and evaluate, even with thousands of words. I sit here and feel like Iâve left out so much of what GTA 6 is.Â

Grand Theft Auto 6 is not the kind of game we get very often. Itâs a massive experience that is filled with more content and more ideas than some entire game franchises.Â

I had high expectations for Grand Theft Auto 6. This much time and money being poured into one video game leads to a lot of hype. Yet GTA 6 surprised me by not just meeting those expectations, but often exceeding them.Â

Jason and Lucia feel like a real couple and are characters that I loved rooting for as they tried to escape the shitty hand they’d been dealt. The world is not just massive but also reactive, and feels the closest a video game has ever gotten to truly recreating all the vibes, life, and details youâd expect from a real place. The action is better than ever, but GTA 6âs quiet moments are really where the game leapfrogs over anything seen in a past GTA entry. And it all comes together to deliver something that truly makes the long wait feel both worth it and absolutely necessary.Â

There were nights when Iâd stay up far too late playing this game, not because I was crunching to finish it before the review embargo, but because I just didnât want to put the controller down.Â

GTA 6 is a truly remarkable game. A masterpiece of open-world design that brings forward the best parts of all of Rockstarâs past games into one billion-dollar adventure that is unlike anything Iâve played before. Itâs a game Iâll be playing for years, and I canât wait to talk about it with others.Â

Document Fraud Detection Vendor: Questions to Ask

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Posted on Nov 18 • Originally published at htpbe.tech

Originally published at htpbe.tech. The version on htpbe.tech stays in sync with the latest detection algorithm — refer to it for the canonical text.

You have a shortlist, a trial window and a meeting where someone will ask which tool to buy. A convincing demo does not show how a tool handles your files. This checklist is for the part after the demo: what the tool’s output means, what happens when it is wrong, and what it costs to find out.

One scoping note first. These questions cover tools that do structural analysis to check whether a file was modified after it was created. Identity verification, issuer verification and checking whether the content is true are different jobs, done by different tools and processes. Structural analysis of the file complements them; it does not replace any of them.

Judge a document fraud detection vendor on three things before the headline features: what its verdict proves and what it does not, how it reports the cases it cannot decide, and whether you can test it on files where you already know the answer. Then check that its data handling and pricing are written down plainly enough to put in a contract. If you are still deciding whether to buy at all, the build-vs-buy question comes first.

Every tool returns a result. The question is what that result is a claim about. A check on the file can tell you whether the file shows evidence of change after it was made. It cannot tell you whether the person is honest or whether the figures on the page are real.

A vendor that answers the second question without hesitating is telling you something useful. A reasonable standard for that answer: content that was false from the start carries no evidence of a later edit, so a file check cannot catch it. And intact means no modification was detected, not that the document is genuine. You want every vendor’s documentation to draw that line as clearly, whatever words it uses.

Some files cannot be judged by a given method. A document made in ordinary office software has no original to compare against. A scan or a filled form can be redone from scratch. Sometimes the file’s history simply cannot be established, and sometimes the analysis does not finish. A tool that forces each of these into ‘pass’ or ‘fail’ is hiding a limit, not removing it.

The last question matters for your own process. An undecided result should lead to a defined step, such as asking the issuer for a fresh copy, not to a rejection. If you want a worked example of reason-based handling, see what an inconclusive result means.

Any automated check will sometimes flag a legitimate file. A vendor that claims otherwise is making a claim you cannot test. What you can test is what happens next.

Treat any confidence label as a description of the evidence, not a guarantee. If a person can be refused on the strength of the result, your own process needs a human review and a way for that person to contest the outcome.

Ask for the answer in writing, separately for each way files reach the vendor:

Your security team will have its own questionnaire. For a worked example of the answers a reviewer should expect, see data handling in a PDF fraud API.

This is the step that tells you most. Build a small set of files where you already know the answer:

Run them all and record agreement case by case, not as a single percentage. Score each file against what happened to it, not against whether you trust it. Look hardest at the disagreements and at how each one was explained. Keep part of the set back and run it only once, after any settings have been agreed, so you are not simply tuning the trial to your sample.

Ask whether the trial runs real analysis. A sandbox that returns fixed sample results is good for testing your integration, but it tells you nothing about detection on your files.

You should be able to work out next month’s bill from the price page. Ask:

HTPBE does structural PDF tamper detection. Here are our answers, limits included.

If you are comparing specific vendors, our side-by-side pages are here: Inscribe alternative, Ocrolus alternative and Bynn alternative.

Ask, but do not let one number decide. A rate measured on someone else’s files tells you little about yours. A trial on your own known cases, scored case by case, tells you more than any headline figure.

No. A tool that checks whether a file was modified answers a question about the file. Whether the person is who they claim to be, or whether the issuer actually produced the document, are separate checks that still need to run.

It should go to a defined next step, such as a fresh copy from the issuer or a manual review. An undecided result is an honest limit of the check, not a finding against the person who sent the file.

Only if the trial runs real analysis on your own files. A sandbox that returns fixed sample results tests your integration, not the detection.

If you are evaluating an integration, the API documentation covers the request, the result fields and the test keys. To run your known cases, see pricing for credits and plans, or check files through the website on pay-per-check.

Exclusive: Wherobots AI agents automate complex spatial data engineering

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Cloud-native spatial analytics and artificial intelligence startup Wherobots Inc. today introduced an artificial intelligence agent that enables users to build and deploy spatial data pipelines using natural-language instructions, reducing the need for specialized programming expertise.

Called Waldo, the agent can discover data sources, generate queries, perform analysis, visualize results and schedule recurring operations. It’s designed for applications involving location-based information such as satellite imagery, road networks, GPS tracking data and geographic features.

Spatial data presents unusual processing challenges because it combines multiple data types, including geographic coordinates, imagery and geometric shapes. Analyzing this information at scale often requires specialized tools and scarce technical expertise.

A recent survey by Global Marketing Insights Inc. concluded that the global geospatial workforce is 10 to 15 years behind in building the skill levels employers need.

Wherobots, which was founded in 2022 by the creators of the open-source Apache Sedona spatial analytics engine, said Waldo can compress development projects that traditionally take weeks into days.

“Waldo is our new agentic interface,” said Damian Wylie, Wherobots’ head of product. Unlike general-purpose AI coding assistants, he said, Waldo can invoke specialized computational engines that can process enormous geographic datasets.

“We’re not deploying some net-new [large language model] under the hood,” Wylie said. “We’re connecting existing LLMs to our product and also giving it the context it needs to speed up that spatial data workflow.”

The agent orchestrates several components of Wherobots’ platform. Its Havasu spatial data and knowledge catalog discovers and prepares public geographic datasets alongside customers’ private information. RasterFlow, Wherobots’ serverless Earth intelligence and inference engine,  processes satellite and aerial imagery using computer vision models to identify features such as buildings, roads and land-use changes.

WherobotsDB executes the resulting analysis using more than 300 spatial functions, while Wherobots Maps visualizes the results. Completed pipelines can be scheduled to refresh automatically as new data arrives.

The distributed processing platform uses existing cloud storage and enterprise data catalogs, including Amazon Web Services Inc.’s Glue and Databricks Unity Catalog, eliminating the need for customers to migrate their data, Wylie said.

In a demonstration, he showed how Waldo could identify the drainage area surrounding Montana’s West Boulder River using geographic and elevation data. The agent located relevant datasets, constructed a geographic representation of the watershed and displayed the results on a map.

The resulting geometry could support subsequent analysis of snowfall, water runoff or changing environmental conditions, Wylie said. Waldo can also process satellite imagery using specialized machine learning models, including Meta Platforms Inc.’s Segment Anything Model 3.

Potential commercial applications include identifying delivery vehicles that deviate from planned routes, assessing weather-related transportation disruptions and analyzing advertising impressions based on billboard locations and mobility patterns.

Wherobots said customer Action Engine Inc. is using the technology to build recurring fleet analytics pipelines and reports that it can deliver new spatial analyses two to three times faster that was possible with manual processes. Another customer used the platform’s distributed computing architecture to reduce a large-scale data-joining operation from approximately a week to less than an hour, said Benjamin Pruden, Wherobots’ go-to-market executive.

Waldo isn’t intended to eliminate human oversight, executives said. Users can inspect generated queries, review geographic visualizations and create Jupyter notebooks to examine individual processing steps. Wylie acknowledged that the technology can’t guarantee accurate results from every prompt.

“That’s an area we’ll invest,” Wylie said. “We’re not at the stage where we’re going to say every prompt is the best quality you’ll ever get.”

Waldo is available in public preview, with agent tokens currently included at no additional charge in Wherobots Professional Edition. Customers pay primarily for the computational resources they consume, with controls to select processing capacity and monitor costs.
