Comolli e l'utilizzo degli algoritmi: non solo Juventus, come sono andate le sue esperienze

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

"Useremo gli algoritmi perché possono dare un vantaggio competitivo sul mercato alla squadra". Non ha usato mezzi termini Damien Comolli nello spiegare il nuovo percorso che intraprenderà col Pisa, dopo l'addio alla Juventus dei mesi scorsi. Un modello, quello legato a dati e algoritmi, che fa parte della carriera del dirigente francese che in bianconero, ma non solo, ha spesso applicato le nuove tecnologie a sostegno delle decisioni di mercato. "Ho iniziato a usare i dati nel 2003, in modo professionale dal 2006", ha proseguito.

70 campionati e 40 mila calciatori monitorati. Questo il metodo Tolosa, oltre 6 anni fa. Era il 2020 quando Comolli prese il comando del club francese, da poco retrocesso. Tutto fin da subito fu affidato alle analisi dei dati e i frutti si videro presto: dopo un anno di transizione, arrivò la promozione in Ligue 1 e pure il successo in Coppa di Francia, con tanto di ritorno in Europa. Prima del Tolosa il suo nome emerse con rumore al Liverpool: ad Anfield chiuse operazioni straordinarie grazie ai dati, come per esempio Luis Suarez. Ma pure flop clamorosi, tipo Andy Carrol o Stewart Downing, giocatori perfetti per la squadra secondo gli algoritmi.

"Utilizzeremo i dati per tutto, dalla selezione dei giocatori alla definizione delle strategie e a conoscere meglio i tifosi", aveva detto nelle prime ore da dirigente bianconero. Alla Juventus però il suo metodo non è stato capito, o semplicemente non ha attecchito. La dimostrazione arriva dai risultati, di campo ma pure dei singoli. Sul mercato estivo sono arrivati i vari Jonathan David, Lois Openda e Joao Mario, oltre a Edon Zhegrova. Calciatori non proprio indimenticabili della storia juventina. Jeremie Boga, fra gli altri, si sta dimostrando valida alternativa nelle rotazioni. Ma resta minimo, l'apporto degli algoritmi sulle sorti della Juventus.

The leaker who broke the news about The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has some not-so-good news about Majora's Mask.

Back in March of this year, known leaker NateTheHate broke the news that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake would be happening this year, alongside a new Star Fox, Switch Sports game, and Switch 2 Edition of Pikmin 4 – as well as no 3D Mario, which is apparently planned for 2027. NateTheHate correctly predicted the Switch 2 reveal date in 2025, but this string of correct info has made him a pretty trusted leaker within the Nintendo community. Which is why this news brings me no joy.

After The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's success, everyone is certain that a Majora's Mask remake has to be coming soon given the game follows up Ocarina's story as well as reuses a ton of assets from the game. In response to a Twitter user asking about the status of a Majora's Mask remake, NateTheHate responds, "Can only comment on Majora's Mask and it's that I've heard nothing to suggest any such project is currently active."

@tennek027 Can only comment on Majora's Mask & it's that I've heard nothing to suggest any such project is currently active.November 17, 2026

Of course, this is an apocalyptic blow to the level of the moon falling on Termina for those who somehow hoped Nintendo would pull a Capcom with Resident Evil 2 and 3 and release a Majora's Mask remake in a year's time.

That being said, I wouldn't lose too much hope. After the success of Ocarina of Time, the easiest win Nintendo could have is to work on a Majora's Mask remake. It happened on the 3DS, it can happen again.

Since 2013, The Legend of Zelda has pretty much been a yearly franchise, with 2022 being the only year since then we didn't get a new game, a remake/remaster, or a Hyrule Warriors game. It's pretty obvious that Nintendo wants to keep the series on people's minds constantly, and one of the easiest ways for Nintendo to keep things up is through remakes, which take a bit less effort than conceptualizing a new game.

I just hope Nintendo stays strong and doesn't listen to the contingent of people who want the timer removed from the game. As someone who saw the Dead Rising series turn into trash with its fourth entry as Capcom made the time mechanics less and less prevalent, and saw people trying to do the same to The Blood of Dawnwalker through modding, I've become a hardcore time limit defender.

Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea Film Festival Forges ‘Strategic’ Partnership With Cairo Film Festival

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea Film Foundation and the Cairo International Film Festival have announced what is being called a “strategic partnership” that will see the introduction of a dedicated Red Sea Film Festival award at the Cairo fest and other forms of collaboration dedicated to preserving the Arab region’s film heritage.

News of the agreement comes after the Red Sea fest — which is most prominent film event and market in the Arab world — canceled its sixth edition, which was scheduled to take place from Dec. 3 to 12. The decision was made following turbulence in Saudi Arabia due to an escalation in its conflict with Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels, who targeted several Saudi cities. Related Stories Here's How to Watch the Troy Trojans vs. South Alabama Jaguars Game Live Online MS NOW Has 2026 Midterm Elections Coverage: Here's How to Watch Election Night Results Live Online Free

The Red Sea fest has said it will return in the fourth quarter of 2027 with a “renewed vision and a program that continues to celebrate cinema and filmmakers from Saudi Arabia, the region and around the world,” according to a press release.

Starting in 2027, there will be a dedicated Red Sea Film Festival Award presented in Cairo to an outstanding film selected from that fest’s program. “The award will further strengthen ties between the two festivals while providing additional recognition for exceptional cinematic storytelling,” according to a statement.

“The agreement will also facilitate greater collaboration in film programming, creating opportunities for both festivals to showcase selected films from each other’s programmes, including productions supported by the Red Sea Fund,” the statement added. “This exchange will help broaden the reach of these films, connect filmmakers with new audiences, and encourage greater collaboration across the regional film industry.”

The Red Sea and Cairo fests partnership will also focus on film preservation and cultural exchange. The two entities will collaborate “on an exchange of restored films, with a dedicated weeklong screening program planned in Cairo following the fest’s 2027 edition,” according to the statement.

The Red Sea Film Foundation has supported the restoration of more than 20 films, including some of Egyptian cinema’s most celebrated works like Youssef Chahine’s “The Choice” (1971), “Watch Out for Zouzou” (1972) and “Love in Karnak” (1967).

“As Cairo International Film Festival marks 50 years since its founding, this partnership opens a new chapter of cooperation between two institutions committed to Arab cinema,” said Cairo fest chief Hussein Fahmy in a statement.

Commented Faisal Baltyuor, CEO of the Red Sea Film Foundation: “Egypt has played a defining role in the history of Arab cinema, and Cairo International Film Festival continues to be one of the region’s most important platforms for filmmakers and audiences alike. We are proud to strengthen our relationship through a partnership that reflects our shared commitment to supporting outstanding films, creating opportunities for filmmakers, and preserving our cinematic heritage.”

Scripts can’t run AI factories: Dell moves cluster management from the server to the rack

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

As artificial intelligence clusters grow to supercomputing scale, the hard part of the AI factory is no longer buying hardware. It is keeping racks, switches, GPUs and cooling running once they are switched on.

That operational burden is reshaping what infrastructure providers sell. Dell Technologies Inc. has spent the past year pushing its AI Factory beyond servers and storage, and customers are now asking for best practices and better tools to stand up and run what they buy, according to Andrew Vaz (pictured, left), vice president of product management for the Telecom Systems Business at Dell.

“What we are seeing is a fundamental shift from procuring supply to actually standing up and running these very complicated AI clusters and data centers,” Vaz said. “One of the interesting things that we’ve seen is it’s actually now impossible to manage these things with just a few scripts, manually, in an old world manner. The toolsets are becoming more important.”

Vaz and Saurabh Kapoor (right), director of product management and strategy for AI compute and networking solutions at Dell, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed supercomputing, rack-scale management, AI observability and why networking sits on the critical path for AI clusters. (* Disclosure below.)

Dell used the conference to introduce Dell OpenManage Rack Scale and Dell Fabric Manager, two tools for running AI infrastructure from deployment through daily operations. OpenManage Rack Scale manages 100,000 devices in its first release, up from 8,000 servers for its predecessor, OpenManage Enterprise, Kapoor explained. Systems such as Nvidia Corp.’s NVL72 racks bundle compute, power shelves, switches and coolant distribution units into one unit.

“OpenManage Enterprise, the previous product we had, was perfect for servers. Server was the unit of compute,” Kapoor said. “But you have seen in the last 18 months, the world has moved very quickly to larger ecosystems and infrastructures. Rack is the new unit of play.”

Visibility is the other half of that equation. Dell’s iDRAC controller pulls more than 320 metrics from every server, and an AI-assist chatbot can query that telemetry through local large language models, according to Kapoor. A single cooling leak can damage millions of dollars of gear, so every layer has to report in, Vaz noted.

“It could be something as simple as, ‘Hey, this transceiver’s about to die that you can’t diagnose with metrics you have today,'” Vaz said. “You need to use AI to go look at it. You need telemetry off the system to go collect all of that, correlate it, run your algorithms on them, train it and understand what’s happening.”

The network is where those pressures concentrate. Dell Fabric Manager turns validated designs built with Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. into deployable blueprints across different network operating systems and silicon. Agentic AI is also reshaping traffic, and enterprise bandwidth is outrunning a projected 3.5-fold increase, Vaz noted.

“We’re getting blown away by it. It’s more like nine to 10x,” Vaz said. “It’s going everywhere: east, west, north, south.”

Anthropic IPO Today: Share Price, Valuation, Revenue and Key Risks

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Log in to access your notifications and stay updated. If you’re not a member yet, Sign Up to get started!

Nidhi is a Certified Digital Marketing Executive and Passionate crypto Journalist covering the world of alternative currencies. She shares the latest and trending news on Cryptocurrency and Blockchain.

Anthropic is set to price its initial public offering (IPO) on November 18, 2026, ahead of its Nasdaq debut on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT.

The company has launched its investor roadshow and is offering 825 million Class A shares at an expected price range of $70 to $78 per share. The IPO has drawn attention because of its size, strong revenue growth and the financial commitments required to support its AI operations.

Anthropic’s IPO pricing is scheduled for November 18, while its shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq on November 19.

The offering includes 801.35 million shares issued by Anthropic and approximately 23.65 million shares sold by existing shareholders. Underwriters also have the option to purchase an additional 123.75 million shares.

The final IPO price will depend on investor demand and market conditions. Investors buying shares after the Nasdaq debut will pay the prevailing market price rather than necessarily receiving the IPO price.

Anthropic could raise up to $64.4 billion through its public share offering. A separate $26 billion private placement involving major technology companies could take total proceeds to approximately $90.4 billion.

The participating companies include Google, Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC.

Earlier estimates placed Anthropic’s valuation between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion. However, the latest offering terms indicate a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.4 trillion.

Anthropic reported $4.6 billion in revenue during 2025 and $33.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026. Revenue for the three months ending September reached nearly $17 billion.

The company has also attracted significant business customers. More than 11,900 organizations spend over $100,000 annually on its products, while approximately 250 spend more than $10 million.

Its net revenue retention rate is around 900%, showing that existing customers have substantially increased their spending.

Despite its revenue growth, Anthropic’s profitability remains a key concern for investors.

The company reported an accounting loss of approximately $100 billion during the first nine months of 2026. A substantial portion of this figure is linked to accounting charges involving investor commitments that can convert into shares as its valuation increases.

Anthropic recorded an operating profit of $974 million in the three months to June but reported an operating loss of $567 million in the September quarter. Higher computing expenses, short-term infrastructure agreements and other costs contributed to the reversal.

Revenue growth also slowed from 144% in the previous quarter to 47% in the September quarter. Investors will be watching whether the company can manage its costs while maintaining revenue growth.

Anthropic has approximately $895 billion in computing and data center commitments extending through 2045. Most of these agreements cannot be cancelled, leaving the company with substantial long-term financial obligations even if demand slows.

The company also relies heavily on Amazon, Google and Microsoft for computing infrastructure and sales. These companies are both investors in Anthropic and competitors developing their own AI models, creating potential conflicts of interest.

These commitments and partnerships will be important considerations for investors assessing Anthropic’s long-term costs and financial risks.

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Semafor says officials are uneasy with the DHS chief’s AI theory for the US tech outages and his football trip.

Markwayne Mullin, US Secretary of Homeland Security.

Some people inside the Trump administration are quietly criticising Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, Semafor reported on Wednesday. The issue is his comments on a run of US tech outages, and a trip he took after last week’s flight ground stop.

Semafor did not name the officials. TNW has not independently verified the report.

The outages started on 12 November with a global Microsoft outage that hit Outlook and Teams. A day later, the FAA halted all US departures for more than four hours after a router failure disrupted air traffic control centres. On 16 November, online banking problems followed at JPMorgan Chase.

On Fox News on Monday, Mullin said a tech contact he did not name thought AI was swamping old systems that could not keep up, according to Fortune.

“I believe that it’s the SI,” Mullin told host Sean Hannity, using the abbreviation for super intelligence.

Other officials have not backed that idea. On Saturday, FAA chief Bryan Bedford said there was no sign of foul play.

“We see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI-related,” Bedford said.

On Tuesday, US intelligence chief Jay Clayton also told CNBC the outages were not a cyberattack, or a plan by a foreign state.

Meanwhile, the FAA has stopped fitting the new Juniper routers linked to the ground stop. It has also switched off those already in use. An FAA spokesperson told ABC News that the agency has not yet found the root cause.

Mullin has also drawn criticism for flying on a government plane to the LSU-Texas college football game the day after the ground stop, the Associated Press reported. He said the skies had already reopened and that he paid for the trip. DHS said he broke no ethics rules.

Mullin is due to testify on Wednesday at the House Homeland Security Committee’s annual worldwide threats hearing, alongside FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia.

Prediction: $200 a Month Invested in SpaceX Could Be Worth This Much by 2035

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Regular contributions can build a meaningful position, while several return scenarios show what a monthly SpaceX investment could become.

A $200 monthly investment in Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +3.16%) might not seem like much. After all, this is a company valued at almost $1.9 trillion. However, if there's one thing that investing has taught me, it's this: Small, regular contributions can add up over time.

Indeed, a $200 monthly contribution alone, before any gains or losses, will total $21,600 in just nine years. Yet the real power of investing isn't just in the contributions; it's also in the returns. Let's see what's possible for someone who puts those contributions to work in SpaceX stock.

First, let's drill down on the details of this hypothetical plan, as they'll become important later. Let's assume that each month, starting in January 2027, a person contributes $200. They use that money to purchase SpaceX stock (via fractional shares). This nine-year plan will run from January 2027 to December 2035, encompassing 108 monthly contributions totaling $21,600 over its full term.

To see what's possible, let's examine a few potential outcomes. For starters, SpaceX stock could deliver no return at all; in other words, a 0% annual return. In this highly improbable case, the account value would be equal to the contribution amount of $21,600. A more reasonable annual return figure might be the stock market's long-term average, 10%. In that case, the market value of the investment rises to $35,023. A 15% annual return results in $45,702. A bullish scenario of 25% annual returns results in $81,412. Finally, a bearish case: A negative 10% annual return results in a final figure of $14,244.

So which of these scenarios is most likely? The answer depends on growth. SpaceX is far more than simply a rocket company. Elon Musk views it as a package encompassing space launch, satellite connectivity, and advanced computing. These areas overlap: Space launch helps build satellite connectivity, while advanced computing makes launches safer, more efficient, and more frequent.

As for growth, SpaceX is growing by leaps and bounds. The company went public only in June 2026, but revenue growth has been exceptional so far. In its third-quarter earnings report, the company delivered 161% year-over-year revenue growth, fueled by its artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

According to Yahoo Finance, analysts expect SpaceX's 2027 revenue to grow to $181 billion, up nearly 270%. If the company can deliver growth at this level, the stock could more than justify its massive valuation. Moreover, profitability could soon be on the horizon. SpaceX's AI compute and its Starlink network both benefit from massive economies of scale. Such assets are very costly to build, but enormously profitable once operational. Consequently, Yahoo Finance estimates that SpaceX will generate $4.06 in earnings per share in 2027, equal to about $52 billion in net income. That would be a massive jump from the roughly $3 billion gain the company will likely post in 2026.

There are bearish scenarios for SpaceX, too. First off, the company's AI investments could backfire. Think of SpaceX as an AI landlord, renting out expensive data center capacity to companies like Alphabet and Anthropic. Therefore, if customers pull back on spending, SpaceX could be left holding very expensive, yet underutilized, data center real estate. In addition, political pushback on the growth of data centers and their energy consumption could further sap demand, leading to disappointing results for SpaceX.

Second, the company's launch business faces several risks. For one, launch delays would have a cascading effect on Starlink, as projections assume a transition from Falcon 9 to the reusable Starship system. If Starship can't deliver the anticipated Starlink V3 satellites, Starship's unit economics would suffer. What's more, even if Starship is otherwise ready to go, regulatory friction could plague its full rollout.

In other words, SpaceX's growth isn't a given; however, I remain optimistic about the company's ability to navigate these and other potential challenges.

Given its massive growth potential, it seems likely that SpaceX stock will deliver solid returns over the next nine years. Indeed, I believe it will outperform the market. That would put my estimate of its annual returns above 10%. To be conservative, let's assume a 15% annual return. Using the earlier calculation, a person could invest $200 a month in SpaceX stock and see it grow to around $46,000.

Granted, this is a hypothetical scenario, and SpaceX stock carries risk.

Nonetheless, a regular savings and investment routine is a clear way to build and grow a nest egg.

MindsEye Developer Build A Rocket Boy Is Suing ‘Several Third Parties’ To Recoup Tens Of Millions To Pay Debts

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Build a Rocket Boy has officially entered administration, following reports in September that the MindsEye developer was permanently closing. Unfortunately for co-CEOs Leslie Benzies and Mark Gerhard, Build a Rocket Boy owes a lengthy list of creditors roughly £62 million ($81 million). So, how does BARB plan to recoup these losses? You guessed it; they’re suing the saboteurs.

As spotted by RedbullCola on ResetEra, an administrators’ proposal—written by Opus Restructuring LLP—went live on Build a Rocket Boy’s Companies House page this morning. It is quite the read, detailing the MindsEye developer’s full list of creditors and exactly how it plans to repay them.

Its two largest debts are owed to the Diamater Dislocation Master Fund, a Cayman Islands hedge fund, and Marvel Rivals developer NetEase. Build a Rocket Boy owes the former roughly £4.2 million ($5.5 million), and the latter over £36 million ($47 million). It also owes ChatGPT owner OpenAI $25, which is a curiously small sum to include.

Of course, the real question is how BARB plans to repay their creditors. The answer: via vengeful litigation. According to the administrator’s proposal, Build a Rocket Boy is still pursuing legal action against the “saboteurs” that co-CEO Mark Gerhard alluded to back in July ’25, a mysterious number of people who he claimed were deliberately working to destroy MindsEye‘s success. In a leaked video, Gerhard stated that he thinks “a very big American company” called Ritual Network, a YouTube and TikTok management agency based in the United Kingdom, are to blame. Content creator Cyber Boi, who was threatened with a “formal cease and desist demand” in MindsEye’s Discord server for releasing a video titled “Leslie Benzies is in the Epstein Files,” is represented by Ritual Network.

Curiously, the administrator’s proposal states that these “detailed investigations” against “a number of third parties” are considered “to be the largest asset of the administration.” That is, of course, if said litigation is successful.

Speaking of litigation, in April, 2026, the Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain (IWGB) announced that several former MindsEye developers had initiated legal action against Build a Rocket Boy for allegedly installing the “invasive surveillance software” Teramind on their work devices.

Why is this relevant all of a sudden? Well, the administrator’s proposal states that Build a Rocket Boy’s “computer equipment that was utilized by staff” has been “wiped” by the company’s IT department. Curious.

BMW's First U.S.-Made EV Is Now Rolling Off The Assembly Line

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The first American-made electric BMW is now being assembled at the company’s plant in Spartanburg, South Carolina. It’s a big moment for the German automaker in the U.S., but it’s just the beginning of a much larger plan, which will include no fewer than six U.S.-built EVs by the end of the decade.

Roughly 70 iX5 electric SUVs are rolling off the assembly line every day, alongside gas, diesel, and hybrid-powered models. All X5 powertrain versions are based on the same architecture, enabling the car manufacturer to share the same assembly line for multiple fuel types.

2027 BMW iX5 production in Spartanburg, South Carolina

Initially, BMW’s goal was to build no fewer than 100,000 iX5s in 2027 in Spartanburg, but that target has reportedly been revised to 60,000, according to Automotive News. The automaker has not provided production volume estimates for the iX5, but a company representative said that roughly one in four X5s will be electric for the near future.

“Currently, the market is looking like 20-25 percent EVs for the immediate three months,” said Kavit Antani, general manager of vehicle assembly. “As the market sees these vehicles come through, it might shift.”

Suppliers have reportedly been given a target of 175,000 EVs in 2028 and 2029, but that’s still a long way from now, and judging from what has happened in the American electric car market in the previous two years, the target could shift significantly.

The batteries that power the new iX5 come from a new plant 15 miles away in Woodruff, where the first mass-produced packs started their journey to Spartanburg to be fitted to finished chassis earlier this week.

The first Gen6 cylindrical cells used in completed packs will be sourced from AESC in China, BMW confirmed for Automotive News, but the German automaker will switch suppliers toward the end of the decade. LG Energy Solution will supply the car manufacturer’s facilities in the U.S. with locally made cells, while Samsung SDI will supply European factories.

BMW is not backing down from its plan to build six EVs in America by 2030. The iX5 is the first, and it will likely be followed by the iX7, iX6, and a performance-oriented iX5 M, according to BMW Blog.

The 2027 BMW iX5 is powered by a 144-kilowatt-hour battery that can be recharged from 10% to 80% in 22 minutes. Its estimated range sits at an impressive 450 miles, while its dual-motor powertrain delivers 570 horsepower and 594 pound-feet of torque. Pricing starts at $79,800.

“Cheating on exams using advanced equipment is no different from stealing the scores of hundreds of thousands of examinees who worked hard. U.S. export controls and Nvidia’s leadership transition remain key watchpoints

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Nvidia’s solid third-quarter results will no doubt reassure Gulf investors that the U.S. chipmaking giant is on course to maintain a healthy growth trajectory despite the resignation of Jensen Huang.

Nvidia reported revenue of $116 billion for the three months to October, up 103% from a year ago, and above Wall Street estimates of $109 billion. It has beaten estimates in each of the last five quarters.

For the Gulf states, which are betting big on AI to help move their economies away from oil and rely on Nvidia’s advanced chips to achieve that, the company’s future success is critical.

Huang’s affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy has heightened political pressure to tighten export controls amid long-running concerns in the U.S. that China’s access to advanced American AI chips could undermine national security.

It is also likely to sharpen scrutiny of Nvidia’s future dealings with the Gulf as part of a broader effort to prevent China from accessing banned American technology via intermediaries.

Such concerns have previously made securing Nvidia’s advanced chips an uphill battle for regional AI champions such as PIF-owned HUMAIN and Abu Dhabi-backed G42.

In July, the U.S. Department of Commerce loosened export restrictions on the UAE so that approved government agencies and entities—including its tech champion G42—can receive advanced computing hardware, including from Nvidia, under broader license exceptions. The new rule set no caps on how many chips or other sophisticated goods can be sold to those entities.

Democratic China hawks have frequently raised the alarm over the large-scale sales of AI chips to the Gulf region, arguing they could give China backdoor access to U.S. technology. Last May, Democratic senators demanded that AI chip deals with Saudi Arabia and the UAE contain adequate guardrails to prevent the leakage of sensitive technology to China.

Both Gulf countries maintain strong commercial ties to Chinese tech entities.

In September, Chinese tech giant Alibaba Cloud announced plans to ramp up its data center capacity and expand localized AI services across the UAE. Meanwhile, in Riyadh, Lenovo unveiled its first laptop made in Saudi Arabia at its sprawling 200,000-square-meter manufacturing facility, developed as part of a $2 billion partnership with Alat, a subsidiary of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF).

In its first policy response to the Nvidia scandal, on Monday the U.S. Commerce Department introduced an interim rule requiring licences for global transfers of AI chips and servers to companies in 22 embargoed countries, including China. The move aims to close a loophole that has allowed Chinese companies to lease Nvidia’s computing power from locations in other countries.

With Democrats holding majorities in both chambers of Congress from January next year, increased congressional scrutiny of Gulf AI deals is likely.

More broadly, the Gulf’s exposure to the volatility in AI stock prices has been further rattled by Jensen’s resignation amid a broader sell-off in AI tech stocks over the past few months, on the back of valuation and investment bubble concerns.

While not all Gulf funds disclose their individual investments, publicly available filings suggest that Gulf sovereign wealth funds, such as Mubadala, have relatively limited direct exposure to Nvidia shares compared to the scale of their investments in other tech firms.

According to the consultancy, Global SWF, Mubadala ranks among the top institutional backers of AI worldwide.

MGX, an AI and advanced tech investment firm backed by Mubadala, holds stakes and has participated in funding rounds for OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, Databricks, GlobalFoundries, Isomorphic Labs, and SpaceX.

Saudi’s PIF-backed AI venture HUMAIN invested $3 billion in xAI’s $20 billion Series E round in February, shortly before it merged with SpaceX.

Global SWF estimates that Mubadala’s portfolio may have declined by $17.5 billion since the onset of the AI selloff at the end of June, largely driven by a more than 50% drop in chipmaker GlobalFoundries’ share price. PIF, meanwhile, is estimated to have suffered a $5.6 billion decline in the value of its AI-related holdings, largely attributable to its stake in SpaceX.

“Indirectly and strategically, Gulf wealth funds are exposed to the current market turbulence,” Sam Winter-Levy, a senior fellow in the Technology and International Affairs program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, told me.

“MGX and other Gulf vehicles hold large stakes in AI labs, data center platforms, and other companies whose valuations depend on the AI boom—and Nvidia, of course, is central to that boom. The Gulf’s national AI strategies are built on Nvidia hardware. I think a prolonged loss of confidence in Nvidia would hit the Gulf relatively hard.”

In a research note published on Monday, London-headquartered Capital Economics warned that the ongoing shakeout in the AI sector is setting the stage for a larger downturn in the U.S. equity market over the next year.

With Nvidia considered a bellwether for the AI industry, its results should help to calm the markets and buoy investor sentiment ahead of Anthropic’s planned listing on Thursday.

You can read my piece here, which takes a closer look at what the potential fallout from the Nvidia crisis could mean for the Gulf’s AI ambitions, particularly in terms of its planned data center buildout.

Abu Dhabi-backed Masdar has completed its $950 million Lockhart Solar and Storage complex in California, marking another major step in the clean energy giant’s growing U.S. renewables push.

With 365-MW of solar generation and 173.7MW of battery storage, the project can produce electricity to meet the annual needs of about 350,000 homes and businesses.

Commercially, the project is backed by a hybrid of long-term power purchase agreements with California utilities and corporates.

The project was developed by Terra-Gen, which is owned jointly by Masdar and U.K.-headquartered global infrastructure manager, Igneo Infrastructure Partners.

Masdar operates a major part of its U.S. footprint through Terra-Gen, an independent U.S. renewables developer and operator, in which Masdar acquired a 50% stake in 2024 alongside Igneo.

Masdar has already invested around $3 billion in renewable energy projects across the U.S., with a portfolio reaching 6.3 GW across onshore wind, solar, and battery energy storage systems as of Sep. 2026.

It is targeting an expansion of its portfolio by as much as 25-GW by 2030, capitalising on rising power demand from data centers, industrial electrification, and expanding domestic manufacturing.

Globally, Masdar is also pressing ahead with its ambition to reach 100-GW of portfolio capacity by the end of the decade.

A strong recovery in global oil supplies helped the market return to a surplus in October, the first time since the outbreak of the U.S.-Iran war.

Inventories climbed by 2.3 million barrels per day (bpd) to 105.4 million bpd last month, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA), as "Gulf exports recovered much faster than global oil demand."

The higher export rates prompted the Paris-based agency to "significantly" raise its expectations for global oil supply for the remainder of 2026, with fourth-quarter estimates now 3.3 million bpd higher.

The IEA forecasts fourth-quarter supply will average 105 million bpd, exceeding projected demand by 1.7 million bpd.

The oil market is "straightening out" and "showing tentative signs of rebalancing,” it said.

It follows seven months of disruption to global oil flows, as the ongoing war choked off shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route that normally carries around a fifth of the world’s oil and gas supplies.

However, Capital Economics sounded a note of caution about the future path to recovery given that the EIA data also shows that the stock of commercial oil inventories in the OECD plunged by 101 million barrels between February and October.

“Rebuilding depleted oil stock inventories–which is key to allowing oil prices to trend lower–will require oil flows sustaining sizeable surpluses into 2027,” it said in a research note published on Monday.

The research firm’s working assumption is that conditions in oil and natural gas markets largely normalize by the end of 2027 and that prices and spreads fall back further.

“But there is an obvious risk that things either fail to improve, or even get worse,” it added.

GTA 6 Will Officially Be Unplayable If PS5 Gamers Skip This Step

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Grand Theft Auto VI is finally less than 24 hours away, and it's difficult to overstate just how much impact the game is set to have on the medium as a whole. For example, a major GTA Online update last year drew hundreds of thousands of players away from other major live service titles, and the effect of the arrival of the new game could magnify that effect significantly.

However, it turns out, console players are the only ones who will be able to find out for themselves for the time being, with a PC release rumored to be coming relatively soon (in the first portion of next year). If you are getting in on the day one action as a PlayStation player, there's something that you'll absolutely need to make sure you get done to get the game working in the first place.

As first reported by Push Square, PlayStation themselves have confirmed that they are releasing an important firmware update for their flagship console, and it's a mandatory download if you want GTA VI to work at launch. They confirmed the revelation via a post on Twitter/X, which reads:

"Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI. Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they’re ready to play on launch day, November 19."

All of this comes at a time when those working at Sony are doing everything they can to improve the security of their flagship console. Hackers are finding new and more ingenious ways to jailbreak the PlayStation 5, largely thanks to AI tools which allow them to analyse and find vulnerabilities much more quickly than normal.

Two weeks ago, Sony pushed out a similar update that was designed to address the most egregious and recent of these methods, but they're fighting a battle that they seem to be losing for a time being. The arrival of GTA VI ups the stakes for the company significantly, as any world in which players can access it for free on the console is one in which they could lose an astronomical amount of money.

The firmware update you're looking for is v14.23.00, and it clocks in at around 1.3GB, so it isn't too significant if you won't have time to get around to patching your console until later.

Outside of that, things are already looking positive for GTA VI, as the release finds itself nominated for the coveted Game of the Year title, despite not even being out yet. That decision has drawn some controversy for that reason, with those who voted for it in the ballot presumably having early access for review and guide purposes.

The reality is that if Grand Theft Auto VI is anything like as good as fans are expecting then it would have been on most Game of the Year nomination lists anyway. It just so happens that this year's TGAs deadline has come at an awkward time, just before its full arrival.

Bitwise seeks Texas Stock Exchange listing for Zcash ETF

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Coinbase Custody would safeguard the fund’s ZEC holdings, while Bitwise Investment Advisers would serve as its manager and sponsor.

Bitwise Asset Management is seeking to list a spot Zcash exchange-traded fund (ETF) on the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE), according to a registration statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

The S-1 filing names TXSE as the anticipated listing venue for the Bitwise Zcash ETF, which would trade under the ticker ZEC. The fund would hold Zcash directly and seek to reflect the value of its holdings, minus operating expenses and liabilities.

Coinbase Custody would safeguard the fund’s ZEC tokens, while Bitwise Investment Advisers would serve as its manager and sponsor.

The Bitwise fund has not begun trading, and its registration statement has yet to become effective. Its proposed annual sponsor fee also remains unspecified. The public filing also follows an Oct. 16 draft that identified NYSE Arca as the proposed exchange.

The filing comes as asset managers continue to expand their Zcash-linked investment products in the US.

Grayscale launched its Zcash ETF on NYSE Arca in August, becoming one of the first issuers to offer investors exposure to the cryptocurrency through a US-listed ETF. Meanwhile, Winklevoss Asset Services filed in October to launch a competing spot Zcash ETF on Nasdaq under the ticker WINK.

Trump lands in China with key meetings with Xi and Putin on the agenda

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

President Donald Trump greets as China's President Xi Jinping welcomes him after Trump steps off Air Force One at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in Shenzhen in southern China's Guangdong Province, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Mark Schiefelbein/AP hide caption

SHENZHEN, China — President Donald Trump landed in China on Wednesday, seeking to reinforce the U.S. status as the world's leading technology power, but a distressing series of technical outages back home has left the administration scrambling to calm the American public.

The issues put the administration on the defensive at a moment when the president wants to project strength and certainty ahead of a potentially complicated trilateral meeting on Thursday with the presidents of China and Russia, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

As he began his trip to Asia, Trump initially had been nonchalant about the outages that left people in the United States worried about accessing their email, checking their bank accounts or safely flying on an airplane.

"It's fine," Trump pronounced on Tuesday from the Philippine capital of Manila, suggesting it was all just a consequence of being a nation that is "big and powerful."

But then the outages involving Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration, JPMorgan Chase and the National Security Agency's communications network began to overshadow Trump's visit. They raised the specter that artificial intelligence can disrupt daily life, as new cyber vulnerabilities identified require software to be constantly upgraded to fix flaws or other security holes, known as patching, which is supposed to improve how the technology runs.

So at the start of the second day of Trump's trip, Secretary of State Marco Rubio stepped in to reassure Americans on Trump's behalf. He told reporters there was "zero" evidence that the outages are connected or tied to rival nations, cyber hackers or criminals.

"Sometimes when you are going in to fix your system because you've identified a vulnerability, it creates a short-term disruption," said Rubio, who is also Trump's national security adviser.

Xi paid Trump a special honor by greeting him on the tarmac after Air Force One arrived in Shenzhen, China, reciprocating a gesture made by the U.S. president during Xi's state visit to Washington in September.

The two leaders greeted each other at the foot of the airplane's stairs in a handshake that became a hug as group of dancers waved flowers and flags. When Putin arrived earlier on Wednesday, Xi did not greet him at the airport despite their longstanding friendship.

Trump has signaled that he wants to take an improvised approach during his time in Shenzhen, the skyscraper-filled tech hub that is hosting world leaders for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. It's a bet that his unscripted brand of diplomacy based on personal relationships can create some kind of legacy to reshape world affairs during his final two years in the White House.

On Thursday, at a first-ever trilateral, Trump said he plans to talk with Xi and Putin about limiting nuclear weapons and bringing an end to the war in Ukraine, which began in 2022 with Russia's invasion. Analysts are not expecting substantive breakthroughs, despite the unprecedented nature of the meeting.

Before the trip, Trump's aides had told reporters that the war in Ukraine would not be on the agenda. But Trump said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opening to resolve the conflict.

"I think it's very close to getting it done," Trump said. "We're going to have a good meeting on that."

Trump also teased the possibility of a private meeting with Putin and a separate sit-down with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Rubio clarified on Wednesday that Trump was "serious" about meeting with Kim as a way of resolving tensions with North Korea. But he suggested no meeting was currently scheduled between Trump and Kim for Thursday.

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., left, walks beside U.S. President Donald Trump during a welcome ceremony marking Trump's state visit to the Philippines at Malacanang Palace in Manila, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Aaron Favila/AP hide caption

Before he landed in Shenzhen, Trump had lunch in Manila with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at the Malacañang Presidential Palace.

Marcos noted that he had sent fried chicken from the Philippine chain Jollibee to the U.S. delegation for a late-night snack Tuesday and complimented Trump for "working very hard."

Trump praised the U.S. bond with the Philippines and the interior decoration of the presidential palace.

"Our people share common history, common values, common interests, common architectural tastes," Trump said. "I love what you've done here."

He said after their meeting that the two nations had reached a trade deal on Wednesday, though he had also said last year that an agreement had been reached. The U.S. trade deficit in goods with the Philippines has risen under Trump, climbing from $4.9 billion in 2024 to $12.8 billion during the first 9 months of this year, according to the Census Bureau.

There were no details about the new agreement, although the White House said it will involve Manila buying more energy and farm products.

Trump also had a short reunion with Imelda Marcos, the former first lady and mother of the Philippines' current president.

Famed for her lavish shoe collection, Imelda Marcos knew Trump decades ago through the New York City party scene. During the 1986 "People Power" uprising, her husband, Ferdinand Marcos, was ousted as the Philippines' strongman leader.

Trump called her "always the most beautiful" and the 97-year-old matriarch appeared to hand him a gift, according to a video posted by the White House.

Russian President Vladimir Putin speaks at the APEC CEO summit held ahead of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, southern China's Guangdong province on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Dmitry Azarov/Pool Sputnik Kremlin hide caption

The prospect of Trump meeting with two of America's largest geopolitical rivals has been a source of unease as the U.S. president has been less welcoming of historic allies such as Canada and NATO partners in Europe.

His tariffs that were intended to curb China's trade surplus have done little to stop the progress of the world's dominant manufacturer, which for the second straight year will have exported $1 trillion more in goods than what it imported.

Even without the digital outages in the U.S., questions about how to handle AI loom over the summit.

The technology is viewed as key to unlocking faster economic growth, but its rapid development has meant it poses national security risks and could evolve in ways that put AI beyond human control.

Trump's close tech industry ally Jensen Huang was recently removed as the CEO of Nvidia after he admitted to an affair with a woman alleged to be an agent of the Chinese government. Beijing has denied that she was a spy, yet the affair raised concerns about how China has been able to access Nvidia computer chips to develop its own AI models that are competing with the U.S.

When asked this week why the U.S. had not been more aggressive in cutting off China's access to advanced computer chips, Trump said there were differences of opinion inside his administration and that "We have a very good relationship with China, and you don't want to insult them."

Trump has said he does not plan to bring up Taiwan, a self-governing island that China claims as its own. Taiwan is the leading manufacturer of advanced computer chips, including those designed by U.S. companies.

Still, Trump expects that Xi will push him on Taiwan's sovereignty.

"I'm sure he'll raise it," Trump said. "I won't have to raise it."

Ukraine allies reject U.S. criticism of deep strikes inside Russia ahead of Trump-Putin-Xi summit

📅 2026-11-18  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Germany and the U.K. have pushed back against U.S. criticism of Ukraine's deep strike campaign inside Russia, underscoring tensions between Washington and European allies over Kyiv's war strategy.

The clash comes ahead of a highly anticipated trilateral meeting on Thursday between U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China.

Geopolitical flashpoints such as trade, artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons are expected to be a major focus of Trump, Putin and Xi's meeting, with external observers closely monitoring any discussion of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Speaking at NATO's headquarters in Belgium on Tuesday, U.S. Undersecretary of Defense Elbridge Colby likened Ukraine's deep strikes inside Russia to a spectacle, adding that they "have not been effective in driving an end to the war, nor do they contribute to blunting Russia's advances on the front line."

The Pentagon policy chief acknowledged Ukraine's mid-range strike campaign using novel drone technologies and tactics to deny Russian advances on the front line has proven "very effective."

He added that Ukraine's Armed Forces gained more territory than Russia for the second consecutive month in October.

However, Colby said Ukraine's deep strikes targeting "civilian infrastructure," citing Russia's biggest online retailer Wildberries, "have actually probably hardened the Russian public's resolve and the Kremlin's own willingness to escalate."

Kyiv has said that warehouses targeted by Ukrainian drones were involved in providing Russian forces with drone components, navigation equipment and other military components. Wildberries and the Kremlin have denied the company is involved in Russia's war in Ukraine.

Asked whether he shared Colby's position on Ukraine's deep strike campaign inside Russia, German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said criticizing strikes designed to destroy strategic military and military-use targets in Russia "is quite a stupid thing, I think."

"Instead of criticizing that, we should rather criticize and talk about the terroristic strikes every night and every day on civil energy, water and heating infrastructure in Ukraine. This is kind of terrorism," Pistorius said at a news conference.

British Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting echoed those comments, saying it is "not for us to tell Ukraine how to fight their war."

He added: "There is no doubt in my mind that it has helped to degrade Putin's war machine, buying time and saving lives."

Trump has previously called on Ukraine to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries and infrastructure used to produce and distribute diesel, saying the attacks were responsible for a global shortage.

Ukraine has stepped up its strikes on Russian oil facilities and logistics infrastructure in recent months, seeking to raise the cost of the war for Moscow after more than 4½ years of conflict.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday lauded an "unprecedented operation" targeting the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea in what marked a symbolic blow to the Kremlin's war effort.

A coordinated drone and missile strike on the bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian forces and is one of Putin's signature projects, damaged the crossing.

In response, Russia said the bridge would be restored and "will be even better than before."

GOP chairman demands answers on Trump's costly VA technology overhaul amid US-wide outages

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

President Donald Trump highlights his administration's efforts to reform the Department of Veterans Affairs, including expanding veterans' healthcare choices and strengthening VA accountability.

Shifting timelines and ballooning costs of the Trump administration's contracts to modernize the federal government, including programs affecting veterans, are raising alarm bells on Capitol Hill.

House Veterans Affairs Committee Chairman Mike Bost, R-Ill., wrote to the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) this month asking for more information on an Oracle software rollout for streamlining employee data and what, if any, safeguards are in place to stop potential data breaches from leaking Americans' sensitive personal information. It comes as the country has grappled with multiple outages hitting the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), big banks, and Microsoft, among other entities.

"I write to you today to express concern about the pace of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Federal Human Resources (HR) 2.0 implementation, uncertainty surrounding VA’s transition costs and readiness, and the risks posed by another major Oracle implementation affecting the Department," the letter said.

"The House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs supports efforts to modernize HR systems and improve how VA manages and supports its workforce. However, modernization must proceed with clear accountability, adequate resources, and safeguards against disruption."

‘BIG BALLS’ OF DOGE FAME GIVES EXCLUSIVE LOOK AT NEW TRUMP MISSION TO OVERHAUL GOVERNMENT

Illinois Republican Rep. Mike Bost speaks alongside Rep. Lisa McClain, a Republican from Michigan, and Rep. Steve Scalise, a Republican from Louisiana, during a news conference at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on Oct. 9, 2025. (Annabelle Gordon/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Technology firm Cerner won a $10 billion government contract in 2018 to modernize record-keeping at VA-run hospitals over 10 years. Cerner was acquired by multinational tech company Oracle four years later.

ORACLE HEALTH DATA BREACH EXPOSES NEARLY 20 MILLION PATIENTS

It was later paused for several years during the Biden administration in an effort to root out performance issues affecting veterans and healthcare providers at VA hospitals, the department said at the time.

Since then, the VA announced earlier this year it would extend that contract through 2031 — with a new total price tag of $27 billion.

OFFICE OF PERSONNEL MANAGEMENT UNCOVERS $500M IN FRAUD AND WASTE IN FEDERAL HEALTH BENEFITS PROGRAMS

It's raised concerns among lawmakers on Capitol Hill, including Bost, who referenced those issues in his questions on the VA's use of Oracle for modernizing its employee data via HR 2.0.

"More than four months after Oracle was selected to provide the governmentwide platform underpinning HR 2.0, the Committee seeks detailed evidence of implementation progress and readiness at VA. In addition, VA’s years-long experience with Oracle’s Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) program reinforces the need for caution," Bost wrote.

A Department of Veterans Affairs sign is displayed outside the Washington VA Medical Center on July 17, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)

Bost also cited system performance issues and problems with user satisfaction with EHRM highlighted by the Government Accountability Office (GAO), but he said only four of GAO's 18 recommendations have been fully implemented as of this past August.

In June 2026, Oracle was awarded a $395.8 million contract to modernize the federal government's human resources systems.

DHS INVESTIGATES MASSIVE DATA BREACH EXPOSING 40,000 EMPLOYEES, INCLUDING ICE AND BORDER PATROL AGENTS

An independent government watchdog "identified inconsistent completion targets, concentrated security and authorization risk, vendor-dependent data migration, and persistent staffing gaps" with HR 2.0 software implementation in October, Bost noted.

"The report describes completion targets shifting from July 4, 2027, to as late as March 2028, while the Wave 2 timeline remains unset," he wrote.

He also raised concerns about the potential for a data breach after the FBI was targeted by hackers in September.

Though he noted existing reports about that hack do not link it to potential issues with Oracle's software at the VA, Bost suggested that staffing gaps and HR 2.0's "centralized authorization approach" could allow for vulnerabilities that need to be accounted for before the rollout is complete.

Fears of tech vulnerabilities are at an all-time high in the U.S. after multiple private and public entities experienced disruptions in service. Travelers were hit with chaos last week after an issue with air traffic control towers caused a nationwide ground stop of flights, while Amtrak's booking system also went offline for several hours.

Just on Monday, major banks like JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America experienced some service disruptions and transaction delays.

The incidents have not been connected so far.

In his letter, Bost also called on more transparency with HR 2.0's funding, warning it should not take away from resources aimed at Oracle's contract on veterans' healthcare systems.

"Identify VA’s projected costs, savings, funding sources, and funding gaps for fiscal years 2027 through 2029," Bost asked. "Explain how OPM and the VA will protect resources needed for EHRM and veterans’ services, avoid duplicative implementation spending, and ensure timely retirement of legacy systems."

When reached for comment, an OPM official told Fox News Digital the office "is working closely with agencies and stakeholders throughout implementation to drive adoption, manage change effectively, and continuously improve the platform over time. We take concerns over data security seriously and also want to highlight that HCM will be leveraging Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM, not PeopleSoft."

BYD vs. Ford: Why the Cheaper Automotive Stock Isn't Necessarily the Better Investment for 2027

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

The global transition to electric vehicles is reshaping the economics of the automotive industry, but leadership in electrification doesn't necessarily translate into superior financial performance.

The global automotive industry's transition toward electrification is creating new opportunities for manufacturers while challenging the profitability of established business models. For investors considering BYD (BYDDY -1.23%) and Ford Motor (F -1.99%), the two companies offer fundamentally different approaches to navigating this transition.

BYD has emerged as a global leader in electric vehicles by leveraging its vertically integrated supply chain and competitive pricing. Meanwhile, Ford continues to rely on its established truck, SUV, and commercial vehicle businesses while investing in electrification.

Although both companies face declining revenue and significant financial pressures, their contrasting business models, capital requirements, and growth prospects could make one a more attractive investment heading into 2027.

With a presence in more than 120 countries, BYD is increasingly looking beyond its domestic Chinese market to drive growth. One of BYD's primary competitive advantages is its vertically integrated business model, which allows it to manufacture critical components, including batteries and semiconductors, in-house. This provides greater control over production costs and vehicle pricing.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $120.4 billion, representing a 4.5% year-over-year decline. Despite falling revenue, BYD generated $4.7 billion in net income, translating to a profit margin of roughly 3.9%. Maintaining profitability is particularly noteworthy given intensifying price competition in China's electric vehicle market and the costs associated with international expansion.

As of December 2025, BYD maintained a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.7 and a current ratio of 0.8. Perhaps more concerning, the company recorded negative free cash flow of approximately $14.6 billion in fiscal 2025.

Ford maintains an established global automotive business supported by a network of more than 8,200 independently owned dealerships. Unlike BYD, Ford's competitive advantage stems largely from its established position in the truck, SUV, and commercial vehicle markets. Its Ford Pro division also provides fleet management, maintenance, and software services, creating revenue opportunities beyond traditional vehicle sales.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $187 billion, representing a 1.4% year-over-year decline. However, Ford recorded a net loss of $7.8 billion, translating to a negative profit margin of roughly 4.2%. The company's deteriorating profitability highlights the challenges of maintaining its traditional automotive business while investing in electrification and navigating an increasingly competitive industry.

As of December 2025, Ford maintained a debt-to-equity ratio of 4.7 and a current ratio of 1.1. While its debt burden appears substantial, a significant portion is associated with Ford Credit, which provides financing to customers and dealerships. Additionally, Ford generated approximately $12.5 billion in free cash flow during fiscal 2025.

One of BYD's primary risks is growing trade protectionism. As the company expands internationally, tariffs and restrictions on Chinese-made vehicles could undermine its pricing advantage and limit access to lucrative automotive markets. Meanwhile, intense price competition in China threatens to compress profit margins, particularly as BYD continues to allocate substantial capital to manufacturing capacity, battery technology, and overseas expansion.

Ford faces the challenge of balancing investments in electrification with the profitability of its traditional vehicle business. Uncertainty surrounding EV demand, government incentives, and emissions standards complicates long-term investment decisions and increases the risk of misallocating capital. Ford also remains exposed to costly vehicle recalls, warranty expenses, and rising manufacturing costs. Additionally, its reliance on truck and SUV sales makes the company particularly vulnerable to weakening consumer spending and elevated borrowing costs.

Ford appears to be the more affordable option based on its lower earnings and sales multiples, which reflect the financial hurdles it currently faces.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

Ford is considerably cheaper from a valuation standpoint, trading at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 6.1 compared to BYD's 13.7. Ford also trades at just 0.2 times sales, while BYD trades at 0.6 times sales. Despite this valuation disparity, I believe BYD offers the more compelling long-term investment opportunity heading into 2027.

My preference for BYD comes down to the direction of the global automotive industry. As electric and hybrid vehicles become more affordable, BYD's vertically integrated business model positions it to compete aggressively on price without relying as heavily on third-party suppliers. Its diverse vehicle lineup and expanding international presence also provide multiple avenues for growth, particularly in markets where vehicle affordability remains a primary consideration for consumers.

Ford's attractive valuation and positive free cash flow shouldn't be overlooked. However, the company faces the difficult task of protecting its traditional automotive business while developing a profitable electric vehicle operation. Although BYD's substantial cash outflows and exposure to international trade restrictions warrant caution, I believe its competitive advantages in battery technology, manufacturing efficiency, and affordable electrification justify its valuation premium over Ford.

Nebius Posted Superb Earnings and Crashed Anyway. Buy the Dip.

📅 Nov 18, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Nebius' post-earnings dip is a compelling buying opportunity for patient investors.

Nebius Group (NBIS -1.02%) stock lost 17% of its value after delivering earnings on Nov. 12, which looks like a good buying opportunity. Broader artificial intelligence headwinds have been dragging down the entire AI trade, with Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia acting as one of the latest gut punches.

The bad earnings reaction does not change the long-term fundamentals, which have continued to strengthen. While Nebius may have negative short-term sentiment, the future continues to look bright, warranting a closer look at current levels.

Naturally, the earnings report wasn't perfect. There were some real issues, but they are short-term problems that the company will solve. For instance, some of the capacity from the $17.4 billion, five-year Microsoft (MSFT -2.27%) infrastructure deal was delayed to Q2 2027. Previously, all of that capacity was supposed to be available by the end of the year.

It's not a problem with Nebius' execution. That's a good thing and a bad thing. The good thing is that when Nebius builds its own data centers, it's usually on time. However, the bad news is that some of Nebius' revenue is tied to colocation sites. In other words, Nebius does not own the facilities for those data centers.

Colocation introduces more execution risks and also increases expenses in the future. Nebius doesn't own the entire stack for all of its AI build-outs in the same way that Iren (IREN -3.57%) does. The company hinted at that in the Q3 shareholder letter, saying that future gigawatts will come from sites it owns while citing third-party delays as a major reason for the shift.

In its Q2 results, Nebius guided for $7 billion to $9 billion in annual recurring revenue (ARR) by the end of the year. The company pushed that target to $7 billion-plus by February and believes it will be in that range before the New Jersey site tied to the Microsoft deal is at full capacity.

This delay caused some concerns and is part of the reason why the stock dropped by 17% on earnings. However, does a delay for this lofty ARR target from December 2026 to February 2027 really mean anything if you zoom out five years?

It's a small snag in timing that does not change the thesis. Furthermore, the delay is due to a colocation facility, and Nebius is increasingly moving away from that model for future AI data centers. The problems are small rather than structural, which makes the current price drop a good buying opportunity.

Some investors were worried about Nebius projecting $40 billion to $45 billion in capital expenditures in 2027, but that's the nature of building large data centers that require AI chips. Some of the best parts of the business model suggest that Nebius can comfortably cover its capital expenditure requirements.

For instance, customer prepayments now cover all of its capital expenditures tied to Q3 agreements. These expenditures include GPUs, data center construction, and leasehold improvement costs, according to Nebius' Q3 shareholder letter. In 2027, 75% to 85% of Nebius' capital expenditures are expected to be covered by prepayments and available investment-grade asset-backed financing.

Nebius' cash balance, credit facilities, and revenue surge may be enough to cover the gap. Its megawatt values continue to climb, with Q3 deals averaging more than $25 million per megawatt, compared to a range of $20 million to $25 million per megawatt in the second quarter.

Rising megawatt values have also reduced the payback period of future deals from 1 year and 10 months to 1 year and 7 months. Trimming the payback period by three months in a single quarter highlights Nebius' strong traction, and this payback window excludes prepayments.

Nebius is targeting $12 billion to $13 billion in revenue next year. It implies that revenue will quadruple from current levels, and if that growth continues, this dip can be a generational buying opportunity.

The new Marvel Comics app is a major improvement over Marvel Unlimited. Powered by Webtoon, this new mobile and desktop app gives you instant access to over 35,000 Marvel comic books, or over 85 years' worth of stories from The House of Ideas. While the new app isn’t perfect, it delivers easier navigation and a slicker interface than its predecessor.

I’m not familiar with Webtoon, but I used Marvel Unlimited for many years, as I detailed in my Marvel Unlimited — here's the 5 best classic comic books to read first article. I’ve used the Marvel Comics app for the past week and have largely enjoyed the experience. This is especially true because I haven’t read new Marvel comic books in a couple of years. The app provides a nice way to catch up where I left off — not to mention reading or re-reading the classics.

Here’s everything you need to know about the new Marvel Comics app, along with my hands-on experience using the app on some of the best tablets.

The new Marvel Comics app offers over 35,000 comics from the company's extensive catalog of Marvel, Star Wars, and 20th Century Studios. The Base subscription costs $9.99 a month or $69.99 a year, while the Ultimate tier costs $12.49 a month or $99.99 a year.

As Marvel detailed when it announced its partnership with Webtoon Entertainment for the new Marvel Comics app, Webtoon built the app from the ground up for mobile and web. Like the company’s own comic book reading platform, the Marvel Comics app lets you discover new and old books faster and makes reading more flexible across devices. The app supports traditional page-based comics (single-issue “floppies”) and vertical-scroll formats, such as Marvel Infinite.

The dynamic cover-scroll interface lets you browse comics right on the home screen and dive into the dedicated Discover section to find specific titles, characters, and creators. You can follow your favorites by clicking the follow button so you don’t miss new books or revisit older titles. The Pull List is especially useful because it surfaces the latest issues from followed series, characters, or creators. There is even an Upcoming Release section that shows which books will be available so you can add them to your Pull List ahead of release.

The Marvel Comics app offers two subscription tiers. The Base tier costs $9.99 a month or $69.99 a year (both plus tax). This gives you access to the full Marvel Comics digital library, with new issues arriving as soon as three months after their print release. The Ultimate tier gives you access to new comics as soon as 30 days after their print release, on top of the full library. This tier costs $12.49 per month or $99.99 a year (plus tax for both).

At first glance, the new Marvel Comics app doesn’t appear all that different from the old Marvel Unlimited app. As before, the interface has colorful comic book covers on a black background. However, the differences become apparent when you take a closer look at the dedicated sections on the Home page.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The Continue Reading section is there as before and is self-explanatory. This lists up to 20 books, so you’ll have plenty of space if you’re reading a lot of them. The Pull List directly under that section shows ma the latest issues from the series, characters, and creators you follow. You’ll find many of these books in the Latest Comics section further below, though this latter one has all the latest issues even if you don’t follow them.

Beyond that, there are several sections featuring recommendations and guides based on what you follow, along with showcases for whatever’s the hottest thing at Marvel—which, at time of writing, is the new Midnight imprint.

I tested the app on the iPad mini 8, iPad Pro M5, Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, and on my iPhone 16 Pro Max. I found that the app was just as snappy and responsive on all of these platforms, which include iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and Android 17. The interface is slightly different on Android, with the Home, Explore, Library, and Account tabs residing at the bottom of the Home page instead of at the top like on Apple devices.

Though I’ve gotten used to it, I find the Home page somewhat cluttered. I think all of the recommendations and guides are fantastic for brand-new readers, but if you’re like me and mainly want to see the new comics, it can be a lot to sift through. This is something that the rival DC Universe Infinite app has mastered, as you get the latest releases and trending series up top and dedicated reading guides at the bottom.

I have mixed feelings about the Explore tab. While it does let you browse through specific books/characters/creators, I wish it were something more user-friendly than an alphabetical list of whatever you’re exploring. Sifting from Amazing Spider-Man to X-Men isn’t exactly streamlined, let alone engaging. That said, typing what you’re searching for (such as Daredevil) brings you to a page with guides and series that are easier to navigate.

Lastly, I wish there were a dedicated settings option so that I could change the background from black to white. Yes, this would make the app appear more like DC Universe Infinite and less "Marvel-y," but having the option would be good, as the all-black background can be eye-straining for me.

The actual reading experience is largely the same as before. No matter which device I read on, drawings and text appear sharp and vivid. Page swipes are fast if you’re reading a full page like I typically do. I don’t often use the guided panel view on tablets, but it’s essential when reading on the iPad mini or my iPhone, since my eyes aren’t what they used to be. When you finish a book, you can then read the next issue or something the app recommends.

The biggest upgrade for me is getting new comics one month after they release physically in comic book shops. Again, I’m trying to get back into Marvel comics, so I want to be as up to date as possible. I also don’t think it’s a coincidence that this app launched a little over a month after the first Midnight books shipped in October. It was certainly nice seeing the new horror-centric takes on X-Men, Fantastic Four, and Spider-Man.

While this is a nice upgrade, I can’t say I’m surprised that the highest tier of the Marvel Comics app offers new books a month after retail. Why? Because this is something the DC Universe Infinite app has offered for over a year. Now, I can be up to date on both of The Big Two’s comics, which is awesome.

It’s still early days for the Marvel Comics app, so I’m sure Webtoon will tidy it up over time. If we can get fewer recommendations on the home page, a more streamlined search function, and the ability to change the background color, I'd be a lot happier.

Now that Marvel Comics has a new CEO, I think it’s the right time to return to the house Stan Lee and Jack Kirby (and many other legends) built. If you prefer reading comics digitally, or don’t want to pay $4.99 for single issues, then the Marvel Comics app is an excellent way to read the latest from Marvel, not to mention revisit your favorite stories from the past.

The $69 Base tier costs the same as Marvel Unlimited’s used to, and is a great way to dive in. If you’re more serious about your comics, the $99 Ultimate tier is well worth it—and also $20 less than DC’s Ultra yearly subscription plan. But whichever tier you get, you’re getting your money’s worth.
